articles.title: Tennessee Titans make changes to practice squad
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans added defensive back Derrick Canteen to the practice squad while waiving two linebackers.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans not only held workouts and added a cornerback to the 53-man roster, but also made practice squad changes.

The Titans brought back defensive back Derrick Canteen, who has bounced on and off the practice squad all season, and waived linebacker Dominique Hampton in a corresponding move. The Titans also waived linebacker Milo Eifler from the reserve/injured list.

This move again reunites Canteen with Saleh, who were together with the San Francisco 49ers in 2025, after he signed as an undrafted rookie free agent following the draft. The 5-foot-10, 193-pound defensive back spent the majority of his rookie season on the 49ers' practice squad.

Canteen is a second defensive back who was brought in by Tennessee on Tuesday, joining former Carolina Panthers cornerback Corey Thornton, who is being added to the 53-man roster pending a physical.

Canteen should be at the facility on Wednesday when the Titans take to the field to start preparations for their Sunday matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: 2027 NFL mock draft 2.0: Jets get aggressive for a QB but it's not Arch Manning who is a top-3 pick
articles.summary: Like in my first mock draft of this season, I still have the Jets trading up to the top spot to get a quarterback. Step on up, Drew Mestemaker.
articles.body:
Here's another mock draft to help fill some time during your holiday travel.

And yes, like in my first mock draft of this season , I still have the Jets trading up to the top spot to get a quarterback.

1. New York Jets (Trade with Tennessee Titans) — Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State

In this deal, the Jets keep the No. 5 overall pick and package the Nos. 4 and 15 picks and a 2028 second-rounder to move up and tab Mestemaker as their QB of the future. Mestemaker has solid size (6-foot-3, 215 pounds) with a good but not overwhelming arm. He plays in a friendly offense that he maximizes with his aggressiveness. He's a loose athlete with a knack for changing arm slots and the arc on his throws. He's had some inconsistent play over the last month or so as his aggression leads to too many dicey decisions. Yet he's the exact type of gunslinger who would be fun to pair with the Jets' assortment of talented young skill players.

2. Los Angeles Chargers — Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

A season from hell can have its rewards!

3. Miami Dolphins — Arch Manning, QB, Texas

I kept Manning in the top 10 of my midseason big board . The shorthand version: he's been inconsistent, but I always come back more optimistic about him after reviewing his film with context in Texas' offense. I am still continuing to bet on Manning's athleticism, size, creativity and ability to navigate the pocket. The Dolphins are having an ideal tanking season of losing games, but they're competing with a well-schemed offense and defense with young players starting to shine on both sides of the ball. Manning would be dropped into a better-than-it-appears situation in Miami with the Dolphins' young and talented wide receivers (hello, Caleb Douglas!) and an already competent offensive line. Veteran center Aaron Brewer would help ease the learning curve, too.

4. Tennessee Titans (Trade with New York Jets) — Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina

Instead of snagging another wide receiver for the improving Cam Ward, now armed with three first-round selections, the Titans plan on finding a pass catcher later in a very good wide receiver class. I have an inkling they bet correctly in this mock, too. The Titans tab the über-talented Stewart, giving head coach Robert Saleh his new version of Nick Bosa to jump-start what has been the league's worst defense.

5. New York Jets — Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame

Loaded already with skill players on offense and a Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate in David Bailey up front, the Jets take Moore to fill the hole left in the wake of the Sauce Gardner trade to the Colts. Moore has size and length packaged with top-end footwork and understanding of wide receiver routes. He can play inside and outside, and completely snuff out the opposition's No. 1 options. The Jets might end up getting an upgrade at corner.

6. Arizona Cardinals — Austin Simmons, QB, Missouri

Yes, the Cardinals went with Carson Beck in the third round in April, but they haven't really seen much of Beck so far to have the signal-caller spot solidified. Instead, the Cardinals go with one of the biggest risers this season to be their quarterback of the future. Simmons can spin the football. His aggression, arm talent and weekly improvement have his stock soaring this year, even if the box score numbers have been up-and-down. He re-signed with Missouri, but with a notable caveat that he is still free to gauge his draft stock . Pairing Simmons with Mike LaFleur in an offense that likes to have its quarterback drop straight back and work from the pocket has me excited about the fit.

7. Tampa Bay Buccaneers — Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana

The Buccaneers desperately need outside options with size to help pop open the offense, even with recent investments at the position. Ted Hurst was drafted in April as a Day 2 dart throw and Emeka Egbuka was drafted the year before that, but Egbuka has struggled with injuries while languishing in this year's morbid Buccaneers passing game. He also might be best as a power slot option in the future who does his best work against zone, like his teammate Chris Godwin Jr. was during his peak years. Becker gives the Buccaneers size (6-foot-4, 208 pounds), a ball winner and a valid deep threat to open up space for their running game and other receiving options. Now the ball just has to get to him.

8. New Orleans Saints — Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson

No more stopgaps for the Saints on the outside. No more Kool-Aid McKinstry being targeted by quarterbacks. Rejoice, Saints fans. Hampton is a big defender who can play in zone but might be best in man-to-man situations. He impacts the game with his size (6-foot-2, 205 pounds) and awareness, and would help solidify the outside cornerback spot for the Saints.

9. Philadelphia Eagles — Jordan Seaton, OT, LSU

Back to the basics of team-building for the Eagles. After a retirement and couple of trades that hit both sides of the ball, Philadelphia is looking to put beef back on the menu. So to the trenches the Eagles go, taking the talented Seaton to be up to the unenviable task of replacing Lane Johnson at right tackle.

10. Atlanta Falcons — Zereoue Williams, OT, Utah

I stewed on taking a quarterback for the Falcons. I then eyed a front-seven player like Chris Cole from nearby Georgia to inject even more talent into Atlanta's defense. But, do the Falcons pursue a veteran option at quarterback this offseason? Or do they really like a quarterback here, even if he's fourth off the board? Jalon Walker was a recent first-round selection with James Pearce taken in the same draft. Do the Falcons select another edge defender (Walker provides different skills than the others, but the question remains) with Colin Simmons still on the board? The Falcons could go with another wide receiver here, too, and I wouldn't fault them.

Instead, the Falcons give themselves a right tackle for next year and a potential left tackle replacement for when the immortal Jake Matthews hangs them up. Williams is twitchy and still developing his skillset playing the position, but he is an easy-moving athlete who can hang as a blindside protector for a long time if he continues to ascend as he has this season.

11. Baltimore Ravens — Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas

The Ravens could go in a variety of directions here and I would totally understand their decision. They instead bolster a position they just spent on in free agency. Simmons is an explosive athlete who is best when he can pin his ears back and get after the passer. Trey Hendrickson is still on the roster and Mike Green has had flashes. Simmons could give the Ravens another needle-moving talent to throw at quarterbacks.

12. Las Vegas Raiders — Jackson Harris, WR, LSU

Brock Bowers can lead a passing game as he's that kind of dynamic pass catcher. But the Raiders need more players to take advantage of Bowers' gravity, and also to help carry the load when he's injured. Harris has been a huge riser this season and is one of my favorite players in this draft. He's a strong-handed receiver who is smooth as a route runner and after the catch. Harris is useful for any type of offense and would complement Bowers perfectly.

13. Houston Texans — Lance Heard, OT, Kentucky

There's a couple of defensive options here that stared at me. The Texans go with Heard, a people mover in every sense of the word. Heard's physical style would fit perfectly in a Texans offense that has started to shift its attack to a more at-you run game.

14. Washington Commanders — Xavier Gilliam, DT, Tennessee

Wide receiver was also in play here for the Commanders, but perhaps Antonio Williams' recent play helped me lean elsewhere. The Commanders go with the explosive Gilliam to add to a defensive front that could lose Daron Payne in free agency this offseason. This will help bolster the spine of Washington's defense.

15. Tennessee Titans (Trade with New York Jets) — Ellis Robinson IV, CB, Georgia

The Titans again provide reinforcements for the league's worst defensive unit. I went with Robinson over Mississippi State's Kelley Jones, despite Jones perhaps being a more traditional fit for what Robert Saleh and Gus Bradley like in their cornerbacks. Robinson is a twitchy player with ball skills. He's not the biggest, but he constantly makes plays on the ball with his burst and awareness.

16. New England Patriots — Trey'Dez Green, TE, LSU

I think this might be the only carryover I had from my first mock draft to this one. And my analysis doesn't really change much: Josh McDaniels likes his tight ends. Drake Maye likes throwing to his tight ends. The Patriots have to continue to add talent to their offense, so any position makes sense here. Hunter Henry turns 32 next month and has slowed down, even if he still is a solid player. Green is a massive target who looks and plays like the former basketball player that he is. He has excellent skills and has developed his strength, which has shown up as a blocker and when working through contact. He's also not stiff getting in and out of breaks and with the ball in his hands. Pairing him with 2026 third-round selection Eli Raridon would give the Patriots a massive tight end room with catching range and athleticism for Maye to fire throws to for years to come.

17. Cleveland Browns (via Los Angeles Rams) — LaNorris Sellers, QB, South Carolina

The Browns throw another dart at the quarterback position. And boy, what a chance of hitting bull's-eye this would be. Sellers is young (important to the Browns process) and has some of the loudest tools you'll ever see at the position. His play has felt more calm and decisive over the past month, but he will need more time, especially in a more conducive situation than the one he's been in the past few years. Landing in Cleveland with the Browns' exciting young group of pass catchers isn't the worst place to settle, especially with head coach Todd Monken, who has gotten the most out of his quarterbacks at multiple stops.

18. Seattle Seahawks — Chris Cole, LB, Georgia

This might be a "race to the podium" type pick for the Seahawks. I had Cole as the 10th overall player on my midseason big board. He's that type of impact player. His range is exceptional and he is constantly around the football. He could be the centerpiece for Mike Macdonald's defense for years to come.

19. Carolina Panthers — Greg Johnson, OG/C, Minnesota

OK, I lied. Here's another carryover from my last mock draft that I just can't help but like. Johnson would help solidify the interior of the Panthers' offensive line that has been ravaged by injuries this season. Johnson's best spot at the next level is center, but his positional versatility would be welcomed in Carolina.

20. Cleveland Browns — Boubacar Traore, Edge, Notre Dame

I peeked at another offensive lineman here, despite this year's Spencer Fano selection and hit on the Austin Barber pick. Funnily enough, I have compared Traore to Jared Verse (but might be leaning more toward a DeMarcus Lawrence comparison). Either way, those are two strong defenders who can push the pocket, and that's exactly what Traore brings to the table. He would be another strong edge defender to add to the Browns' front.

21. Pittsburgh Steelers — C.J. Carr, QB, Notre Dame

Carr is a heady player who constantly finds the right answers with the football. He is an accurate thrower with a quick and consistent throwing motion, a combination of attributes that will give him plenty of fans at the next level. Carr would be a clean fit with Mike McCarthy because of his quick decision-making and McCarthy's more traditional West Coast offense.

22. Dallas Cowboys (via Green Bay Packers) — Kelley Jones, CB, Mississippi State

Even with the Joey Porter Jr. trade and Daron Bland contract, the Cowboys want to inject even more talent into their defensive back room. Something up the defensive spine, at all three levels, could be in play here, too. I went with the long and rangy Jones to give the Cowboys another player to throw at the cornerback position.

23. New York Giants — Jadan Baugh, RB, Florida

The Giants have been itching to upgrade their running back room. They flirted with adding Jonathan Taylor at the trade deadline and even had a foray with Najee Harris this season. Baugh would immediately help the Giants' run game get back on track. He's not the most explosive athlete, but he has size (6-foot-1, 225 pounds) and runs with balance and patience to help his blockers out. He's a perfect back for a Greg Roman offense. I've compared him to a super-sized version of current Giants running back Devin Singletary.

24. Cincinnati Bengals — Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa, LB, Notre Dame

If you've watched the Bengals this year, a couple things stand out. Wow, that offense can score. And wow, the other offenses seem to complete a lot of passes between the numbers. Viliamu-Asa is a hammer who would give the Bengals physicality and more awareness over the middle of the field.

25. Philadelphia Eagles (via Jacksonville Jaguars) — Will Echoles, DT, Ole Miss

More beef for the Eagles! I almost went with another offensive lineman here. Instead, I went to the defensive side of the ball. Echoles is a uniquely built (6-foot-3, 315 pounds) but powerful defender who plays with quick hands. He is a disruptive player wildly different from Jordan Davis, winning with quickness and able to fulfill a variety of roles along the defensive front.

Chambliss or Darian Mensah were considered here. Chambliss is an atypically built quarterback with a unique background to match. He has arm talent and can put real RPMs on the football. Some of his best attempts are throws that he drove over the middle of the field on third down or in the red zone. He's had some shaky weeks recently but I think he's worth taking a chance on because of his work from the pocket and ability to create. And it's the Vikings who decide to take another stab at the position.

27. Kansas City Chiefs — Reed Harris, WR, Arizona State

The surprisingly competent play of Kahlil Benson has the Chiefs deciding to not look at tackle again in the first round. The Josh Downs trade has had promising early returns. Yet the Chiefs will look to add size with even more speed to the receiver spot. Harris is a vertical threat with ball skills and surprising bend given his large frame (6-foot-5, 220 pounds). He has been productive throughout the year and would give the Chiefs' offense an outside threat it has desperately needed for years.

28. Tennessee Titans (via Chicago Bears) — Nick Marsh, WR, Indiana

Marsh is a sure-handed option any quarterback would love to have. He can play inside and out, with real blocking chops to be featured as a power slot option. He has vertical ability, strong hands on the outside and has a feel working against zone. He would fit in any type of offensive scheme and would give Cam Ward another reliable option to grow with.

29. Detroit Lions — KJ Bolden, safety, Georgia

Bolden plays with his hair on fire and would be a perfect fit for the Lions under head coach Dan Campbell. With Brian Branch slated to hit free agency this offseason and Kerby Joseph recently returned from a knee injury, the Lions plop another impact player on the back end of their defense.

30. Denver Broncos — Tae Johnson, safety, Notre Dame

Johnson has battled a foot injury this year, but it looks like he will return soon . He is a hyperathletic and rangy defender who can impact the game in a variety of ways (watch his outing against Pittsburgh last year). Talanoa Hufanga is the only veteran starting safety signed through 2027, so Johnson fills a need while giving the Broncos' defensive backfield another dynamic player.

31. San Francisco 49ers — Trevor Lauck, OT, Iowa

"No, this is the draft where the 49ers will take an offensive lineman in the first round."

32. Buffalo Bills — Anthonie Knapp, OG, Notre Dame

Wide receiver seems to always be an option when discussing the Bills. A defensive back of some sort is another spot I looked at here. The Bills instead bolster their offensive line with Knapp to be their long-term option at left guard.

articles.title: Ranking the Top 10 Thanksgiving Performances in NFL History
articles.summary: It's time to give thanks, football fans. The NFL is back with holiday action and a thrilling three-game Thanksgiving slate.
articles.body:
It's time to give thanks, football fans. The NFL is back with holiday action and a thrilling three-game Thanksgiving slate.

The Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears will serve up a delicious dish in the early afternoon before the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles provide the second course. For dessert, fans will get a pivotal battle between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs.

Along with playoff-relevant games, Thursday could bring a side of memorable performances.

While hundreds of NFL games have been played on Thanksgiving over the years, certain individual outings have stood out above the rest. Here, we'll rank the top 10 Thanksgiving performances in league history based on factors like statistical production, game implications and historical significance.

Stat line: Eight catches for 180 yards and two touchdowns

The Lions were the first NFL team to claim Thanksgiving, but the Cowboys have been a Turkey Day staple since 1966.

Over the years, many Dallas stars have provided memorable performances. Wide receiver Amari Cooper delivered one of the best performances in recent memory in 2018.

Dallas started the season 3-5 that year but battled back to 5-5 ahead of a Thanksgiving matchup against Washington.

Cooper, in his first season with Dallas, helped the Cowboys secure a critical win in front of a national audience with 40- and 90-yard touchdown receptions. He finished with eight receptions for 180 yards and two scores in the 31-23 victory.

Both of Cooper's touchdowns came in the third quarter and helped turn a three-point deficit into an 11-point lead. The Cowboys held on to win, claimed the NFC East title that season, and advanced to the divisional round with a postseason victory over the Seattle Seahawks.

Stat line: Three catches for 163 yards and three touchdowns

The Dallas Cowboys had a chance to take future Hall of Fame receiver Randy Moss in the 1998 draft. Several other teams also passed on Moss before the Minnesota Vikings selected him with the 21st overall pick.

Later that year, Moss and the Vikings met the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. The then-rookie gave everyone a glimpse of what kind of playmaker he could be.

Moss caught only three passes from Randall Cunningham on that day, but he made them count. The Marshall product scored touchdowns of 51, 56, and 56 yards, finishing with a game-high 163 receiving yards.

With just three catches, Moss was the star receiver in a contest that also featured Cris Carter and Michael Irvin, though all three topped 130 receiving yards.

Minnesota wound up winning 46-36 and went on to finish with the NFC's No. 1 seed. Moss was later named the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year and a first-team All-Pro.

Stat line: Nine catches for 122 yards and four touchdowns

Sometimes, even a top performance isn't enough to get the win. Such was the case in 1994, when Green Bay Packers wide receiver Sterling Sharpe nearly willed his team to a victory but fell just short.

Sharpe accounted for all four of Green Bay's touchdowns on Thanksgiving that year, catching scores of one, five, 30, and 36 yards from quarterback Brett Favre. He finished with nine catches for 122 yards and accounted for nearly half of Favre's passing yards.

Despite falling just one receiving touchdown short of tying the single-game record, Sharpe couldn't deliver the victory for the Packers. The Cowboys rallied from a 17-6 halftime deficit thanks to terrific performances by backup quarterback Jason Garrett and star running back Emmitt Smith.

The Packers ultimately lost the game 42-31, but Sharpe put together one heck of a highlight reel for his Hall of Fame resume.

Michael Irvin Talks Cowboys, Super Bowl, Packers vs. Rams and Miami QB Mensah in B/R Interview

1 Thing Every NFL Fanbase Should Be Thankful For 🙏

Stat line: Four catches for 124 yards and two touchdowns, three kick returns for 50 yards, two punt returns for 113 yards and one touchdown

Lions fans have largely enjoyed watching their team on Thanksgiving in recent years, though Detroit hasn't always come out on the winning side. The Lions actually hold a record of just 38-46-2 on the holiday. Their 1986 loss was particularly painful.

Detroit engaged in a shootout with the rival Packers on November 27 of that year. The Lions led late in the fourth quarter but lost it when receiver/returner Walter Stanley took a punt back 83 yards to score the go-ahead touchdown with just 41 seconds remaining.

Stanley also caught two touchdown passes during the back-and-forth battle, recorded 124 receiving yards, and finished with a whopping 287 all-purpose yards.

Green Bay won 44-40, though it was one of the few bright spots of its season. The Packers went just 4-12 in 1986, finishing one game behind the 5-11 Lions.

Stat line: 15-of-23 for 207 yards, six touchdowns and one interception

Bob Griese might not be the most famous quarterback in Miami Dolphins history, but the Hall of Famer had a very prolific career. He was part of Miami's undefeated 1972 season, won two Super Bowls with the Dolphins, and was one of the biggest stars of the Don Shula era.

Griese also achieved an incredible feat on Thanksgiving in 1977. In a lopsided game against the then-St. Louis Cardinals, he threw a whopping six touchdown passes, one shy of the all-time record set by Sid Luckman in 1943.

More than a third of Griese's 15 completions went for touchdowns in the game, as Miami rolled to a 55-14 blowout victory. Griese also threw more than a quarter of his league-high 22 touchdown passes in 1977 on that day.

The Dolphins scored eight touchdowns in the game, which was a franchise record until 2023. That's the same number of incompletions Griese had during his sensational performance against St. Louis.

Stat line: 23-of-28 for 236 yards, six touchdowns and zero interceptions

Many NFL fans still consider Peyton Manning the greatest quarterback ever, for good reason. The longtime Indianapolis Colts and Denver Broncos star had a prolific 17-season career. Along the way, he rewrote the record books and redefined how a quarterback could command a game.

Manning finding time to deliver one of history's most memorable Thanksgiving performances should be unsurprising, really.

Indianapolis' 41-9 win over the Lions in 2004 wasn't much to remember, aside from Manning matching Griese's mark with six touchdown passes while playing to near-perfection.

Manning finished 23-of-28 for 236 yards and the six scores—three each to Marvin Harrison and Brandon Stokley—with a 141.4 quarterback rating. The win was Indy's fourth in an eight-game winning streak. The Colts went on to finish as the AFC's No. 3 seed with a 12-4 record.

Stat line: One interception (returned for a 97-yard touchdown), one sack, one forced fumble

Lawrence Taylor was the most feared defender of his generation for a reason. The New York Giants' pass-rushing linebacker was capable of taking over games in a way that few defenders have since.

The Lions learned this firsthand on Thanksgiving in 1982 , when Taylor came off the bench and almost single-handedly delivered a victory over New York.

The reigning Defensive Player of the Year didn't start the game because of a knee injury. But once he got on the field late in the second quarter, he created havoc.

Taylor harassed quarterback Gary Danielson throughout the game, logged one sack, and forced one of Danielson's three interceptions with heavy pressure. He also ended a promising Detroit drive by picking off Danielson and returning it 97 yards for the game's only touchdown.

The Giants won 13-6 and notched their first victory of the season thanks to Taylor's outstanding performance.

Stat line: 29 carries for 273 yards and two touchdowns

The Lions earned a win on Thanksgiving in 1976 despite a historic effort by Buffalo Bills running back O.J. Simpson.

The former USC star did what he could to get the struggling Bills into the win column at the Pontiac Silverdome that day. He ran the ball 29 times for an NFL-record 273 yards and both of Buffalo's touchdowns.

Simpson broke his own record of 250 rushing yards. However, the new mark would stand for less than a year before Walter Payton reached 275 against Minnesota. To this day, no running back has reached 300 yards in a game, though Adrian Peterson (296), Jamal Lewis (295) and Jerome Harrison (286) have come close.

Buffalo couldn't keep pace with Detroit and lost the game 27-14. The Bills finished the 1976 season with only two wins, though Simpson led the league with 1,503 rushing yards.

Stat line: 10 catches for 303 yards and one touchdown

The early years of the NFL featured a run-heavy game with less downfield passing. However, while quarterbacks didn't dictate contests the way they do today, they still put up outstanding aerial performances 80 years ago.

Take Jim Benton's performance against the Lions on Thanksgiving in 1945. The Cleveland wide receiver caught 10 passes from quarterback Bob Waterfield for an unfathomable 303 yards and a touchdown.

Benton accounted for nearly all of Waterfield's 329 passing yards and became the first player in NFL history to record 300 receiving yards in a game. He held the single-game receiving record for 40 years before Stephon Paige reached 309 against the San Diego Chargers in 1985. Flipper Anderson of the Los Angeles Rams now holds the record with 336 yards, which he set in 1989.

Benton's Cleveland Rams outlasted the Lions 28-21 and went on to win their first NFL championship less than a month later.

Stat line: Six carries for 42 yards and six touchdowns, four extra points

Back in 1929, the Cardinals resided in Chicago and served as cross-town rivals with the Bears. The two Windy City squads faced off on November 28 that year in one of the era's most memorable games.

The contest certainly wasn't memorable for Bears fans, as the Cardinals won in a 40-6 rout. However, the contest featured one of the most incredible performances we've ever seen.

Cardinals fullback Ernie Nevers scored all 40 of his team's points, setting an NFL record that will probably never be broken .

According to the Pro Football Hall of Fame , Nevers ran for six touchdowns against the Bears and added four extra points. He finished with as many touchdowns as the Bears had points. (They scored on a Gardie Grange 60-yard touchdown reception.)

Nevers might not be a household name now, but he still owns a piece of the record for rushing touchdowns in a single game (tied with Alvin Kamar a and holds the record for consecutive points scored (59) across a multi-game stretch. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame as part of its inaugural class in 1963.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes vs Josh Allen: Who will win the NFL's biggest game of the season? Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills headline blockbuster Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Watch the NFL's Thanksgiving triple-header live on Sky Sports from 5pm on Thursday, starting with Chicago Bears at Detroit Lions, followed by the Philadelphia Eagles against the Dallas Cowboys and Patrick Mahomes' Kansas City Chiefs vs Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills from 1.20am on Friday
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen will face off for the 11th time when they headline the NFL's Thanksgiving schedule on Thursday night, live on Sky Sports from 1.20am in the early hours of Friday .

Once more they are positioned neck and neck at the forefront of the NFL's playoff race, once more they will trade the greatness that has governed football for the best part of a decade.

Together they have forged modern football's answer to Tom Brady vs Peyton Manning. Two generational quarterbacks, dictating one another's story, time and time again, although Allen would prefer if the outcome had been a little more even by now.

Mahomes, the driver of a Chiefs dynasty and so often the AFC's Super Bowl gateway; and Allen, the starved nearly man banging down on the Championship door only to see dominant talent blunted by his Kansas City counterpart.

Last season's Thanksgiving Day match-up between the Chiefs and the Dallas Cowboys became the most-viewed regular-season NFL game in history with an audience of 57.230 million. This might well shatter that.

Allen arrives 5-1 in their regular-season head-to-head record, while Mahomes leads the rivalry 4-0 where it matters most - in the playoffs. Five of their last six match-ups have also been decided by one score, their most recent seeing the Bills win 28-21 in November 2025.

Mahomes and the Chiefs defeated Allen's Bills in the postseason four times from 2020-2024, including two AFC Championship Games and two Divisional Round match-ups. And when the Chiefs missed out on the playoffs for the first time since 2014 last season, Buffalo failed to capitalise.

Football swings in waves by way of a league that craves parity and a system structured for the purpose of emerging contenders, new storylines, fresh obstacles, unpredictable risers and fallers.

But every once in a while sport throws in a notion of consistency, an unwavering narrative that shall assert itself as the spine of an entire chapter in its history; Mahomes and Allen remain that constant at the forefront of league discussion and debate.

Who is the best? Who is No 1? Mahomes boasts the resume with three Super Bowl rings, five Super Bowl appearances, seven straight AFC Championship Game appearances from 2018-2024 and the angle-defiant, off-script absurdity to arm talent challenging every boundary in the game during that period.

But while Allen lacks the same accolades, the frequency at which he has carried his Bills outfit through the air and on the ground in critical moments as football's most obvious decider, equaliser and game-wrecker has tossed him into perennial MVP status; there may be no team who struggles as dearly were they to lose their quarterback than the Bills with Allen.

Their rivalry is perhaps best epitomised by January 2022's iconic 13-second miracle. With 1.54 remaining Mahomes connected with Tyreek Hill for a 64-yard touchdown, before Allen hit back with a scoring strike to Gabriel Davis that would see Buffalo lead 36-33 with... 13 seconds left.

The game was over. Until it wasn't. Until teams across the NFL were frightened into ever believing they had beaten Mahomes and his Chiefs until the clock hit zero. It was the greatest lesson in the importance of aggression against a team that, at its peak, thrived in the face of shoot-outs.

Mahomes connected on passes to both Hill and Travis Kelce to put the Chiefs in field goal range, where Harrison Butker broke Bills hearts with a 49-yard kick to send the game to overtime. Kansas City would win the toss and then the game as Mahomes returned to Kelce for the deciding touchdown. Allen had been 13 seconds from the AFC Championship Game, but for those pesky Chiefs.

The Bills are 9-1 as they prepare to host the first game between the two teams at Buffalo's new Highmark Stadium, where the Chiefs will arrive 8-2 in their bounce-back season after last January's playoff omission.

Mahomes and the Chiefs have rediscovered the offensive spark absent for the last two or three years, their quarterback feasting on the back of last December's season-ending surgery-requiring knee injury and Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III having ignited Andy Reid's attack since signing in free agency.

The Chiefs offense ranks No 1 in yards per game through 10 weeks, while sitting fourth in passing, fifth in rushing and seventh in scoring following Sunday's 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

Mahomes has thrown for a sixth-most 2,709 yards for 22 touchdowns to just four interceptions with a third-ranked passer rating of 108.3. With Sunday's performance he has now gone four straight games without throwing a pick, while combining for 1,235 yards and 13 touchdown passes.

He has looked a scary reminder of his former self with tight-window aggression, off-platform invention and out-of-structure magic to enter the Comeback Player of the Year race.

Allen is, meanwhile, riding a six-game winning streak without, in his eyes, playing his best football. He has gone 194 of 302 passing (64.2 per cent) for 2,527 yards and 14 touchdowns to nine interceptions with a passer rating of 93.5, having thrown two picks in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Miami Dolphins.

Allen also leads all quarterbacks with 290 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the ground, though he played a full game without attempting to run the ball for the first time in his career at the weekend.

While it will be the two quarterbacks who take centre stage, defining factors lie elsewhere. Particularly on the ground.

Walker III has again been ruled out with a groin injury after spearheading the Chiefs with 872 rushing yards and seven touchdowns in eight games. But his replacement, fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson, has emerged as a key contributor with 56 touches, 314 yards and three touchdowns over two weeks.

In the opposite backfield James Cook remains instrumental to Joe Brady's Bills attack with 1,060 rushing yards (second in the NFL) for 10 touchdowns from 209 carries. He enters Thursday having rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in an NFL-record nine successive games, and has now surpassed 1,000 yards in four straight campaigns.

Buffalo's prime question marks this season came on defense and whether they had the unit and the personnel to stop football's best teams in the playoffs.

They hired Jim Leonhard as their new defensive coordinator during the offseason and currently rank 11th in total yards allowed and ninth in scoring having not allowed a touchdown in 43 drives since Derrick Henry's rushing score in their win over the Ravens on November 1, albeit having played the Vikings, Jets and Dolphins since then. Still, it can be considered progress for a defense that shipped 28.5 points on average across the first six games.

Steve Spagnuolo's Chiefs defense is, meanwhile, fifth in yards allowed and second in scoring to underline what is currently one of football's most complete teams.

With that being said, the Chiefs' only win against a team with a winning record through 10 weeks was back in Week One against the now 8-2 Denver Broncos.

The Bills have played just two teams sitting among the 14 available playoff spots in the Detroit Lions and the Minnesota Vikings, while their last four outings have seen them encounter back-up or third-string quarterbacks in Miami's Kyle McCord, the New York Jets' Cade Klubnik, Minnesota's Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer and Baltimore's Joe Fagnano, who replaced Lamar Jackson following his thumb injury on the first play from scrimmage in Buffalo's 36-10 win.

"You can see Mahomes stand with more conviction in the pocket. He's not as skittish in the pocket as he was initially, which is natural when you're coming back from a lower leg injury like he had," said Sky Sports NFL's Jeff Reinebold.

"Greg Rousseau and Ed Oliver are going to have to dominate the line of scrimmage. That's one place on the field that I would say Buffalo's defense has an edge against Kansas City. Rousseau is having a tremendous year as an edge rusher. They're going to have to find answers for him. And then Ed Oliver gives them that inside push that you always want to have against Patrick Mahomes.

"I think that's going to be the key because I don't know if Buffalo's back end is built to cover the Kansas City receivers and primarily I think Kelsey's going to be the biggest factor because Buffalo plays a lot of zone and when you play a lot of zone, Kelsey can have a night against you."

Kansas City's wake-up call was in Week Seven when they suffered a 20-3 loss to the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Mahomes and co now enter a defining period of their own campaign with Matthew Stafford and Myles Garrett's Los Angeles Rams, Joe Burrow's Cincinnati Bengals and Brock Purdy's San Francisco 49ers coming up before the end of the year.

Mahomes leads the NFL with 33,267 passing yards since Allen's first full season as starter in 2019, with the Bills quarterback ranked third behind Jared Goff with 2,640. In that same period Mahomes is first with 239 passing touchdowns followed by Allen's 224, while Allen tops all quarterbacks with 92 wins (126 games) to Mahomes' 90 (119 games).

It is perfectly-scheduled and perfectly-poised as a test of who both teams are entering the home stretch towards the playoffs. It could be the best Thanksgiving Day game ever. It might be the most-watched regular-season NFL game in history.

Watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs and Super Bowl LXI on Sunday February 14, 2027. Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free with NOW.

articles.title: Biggest Sleepers at Every Position for Week 12 Fantasy Football 2026
articles.summary: Every NFL team is in action for Week 12, so fantasy football managers don't need to worry about replacing idle bench players. Still, with key injuries and potential late-season breakout players, there are sleepers worth starting this week.
articles.body:
Every NFL team is in action for Week 12, so fantasy football managers don't need to worry about replacing idle bench players. Still, with key injuries and potential late-season breakout players, there are sleepers worth starting this week.

Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is out for the season, and fellow wideout Davante Adams is still recovering from hamstring surgery. Also, second-year tight end Terrance Ferguson is out for the rest of the year. Matthew Stafford has to throw to someone, and it's probably one of the available veteran tight ends; pick up one or both for Wednesday's game.

Despite the Dallas Cowboys' change in defensive play-caller, they're still an appealing fantasy target in the second game on Thanksgiving.

Looking ahead to Sunday, a New York Jets quarterback-tight end stack could produce big numbers for the second time this season against the same opponent. Also, two rookie wide receivers have major upside in advantageous matchups.

Here are our biggest fantasy football sleepers for Week 12. They're available in at least 50 percent of leagues, according to FantasyPros ' consensus roster percentages.

QB Geno Smith at Miami Dolphins (19 Percent Rostered)

In 11 games, Geno Smith has thrown for three touchdowns three times, including one outing against the Miami Dolphins in Week 7. The New York Jets lost that game 28-25, but he finished as QB5 in fantasy scoring.

Smith grew up in South Florida, so he may have family and friends in attendance for this matchup. Aside from that, the 36-year-old is the last quarterback to throw for at least three touchdowns against the Dolphins.

After Smith's three-touchdown passing performance against the Los Angeles Chargers, managers should ride his hot hand as he returns to familiar territory. Smith is primed for another top-10 fantasy scoring finish at his position.

QB Joe Milton at Dallas Cowboys (7 Percent Rostered)

Philadelphia Eagles' third-string quarterback Joe Milton hasn't thrown a touchdown pass in two starts, and he's only completing 52.7 percent of his pass attempts.

However, Milton should be more productive on Thanksgiving, after posting modest stat lines against the New York Giants and Pittsburgh Steelers.

Last week, the Dallas Cowboys defense showed improvement under new play-caller Mike Pettine, but they still allowed Cam Ward to throw for 248 yards and two touchdowns. Even if the Cowboys blow the doors off the Eagles, Milton can rack up garbage-time numbers as Ward did last week.

Also, Milton poses a threat on the ground. He didn't show it against the Steelers, but he ran for 64 yards against the Giants in Week 9. With some rushing productivity, Milton just needs to throw for 200 yards and a touchdown to post a solid fantasy stat line.

RB Chris Rodriguez Jr. vs. Tennessee Titans (28 Percent Rostered)

Last Sunday, running back Bhayshul Tuten struggled to stay on the field because of ankle and foot injuries. He logged 10 carries for 33 yards and caught three passes for 20 yards. The Jacksonville Jaguars could rest him against the Tennessee Titans. Two weeks ago, they dismantled the Titans 40-23.

Even if Tuten plays Sunday, he may have a reduced role, allowing Chris Rodriguez Jr. to handle more carries.

As the Jaguars' No. 2 running back, Rodriguez has four rushing touchdowns and has taken 37.5 percent of the red-zone carries this season. He's a viable short-yardage ball-carrier who could see an expanded role against the Titans' 25th-ranked run defense.

Either because of Tuten's absence or a positive game script in which the Jaguars build a commanding lead, Rodriguez should have a sizeable role and a good chance to reach paydirt.

Rodgers Claims McCarthy Fell Asleep in Meetings

James Harrison Backs Up Rodgers' Stories

RB Justice Hill at Houston Texans (26 Percent Rostered)

Make sure Justice Hill isn't available in your point-per-reception leagues. He has strong boom potential as a ball-carrier and pass-catcher.

Over the previous three weeks, Hill has had explosive runs for 36 and 65 yards and a 25-yard reception, scoring in two of those contests. He's seen at least five targets in three of his last four outings.

If the Baltimore Ravens continue to drift further out of the playoff picture, they'll likely feature Hill more than 32-year-old Derrick Henry. Even though Hill is 29, he's not a downhill ball-carrier and takes less physical punishment in his complementary role.

With double-digit touches in two of the previous three weeks, Hill's workload is trending up. Despite a middling matchup with the Houston Texans, his change-of-pace role makes him a flex option.

WR Antonio Williams at Arizona Cardinals (31 Percent Rostered)

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , free agent Brandon Aiyuk's "most likely landing spot" is with the Washington Commanders. He'll meet with the team on Wednesday, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

So, this might be the last week in which rookie third-rounder Antonio Williams is the clear-cut No. 2 wide receiver. Given Aiyuk's history with quarterback Jayden Daniels, dating back to their college years at Arizona State, the Commanders will likely elevate the talented receiver to the active roster if they sign him.

At least for another week, Williams will be a primary option in the Commanders' passing game, coming off a career-best nine catches for 122 yards.

He draws a plus matchup against the Arizona Cardinals' 20th-ranked pass defense, which has allowed 25 touchdowns, the most in the league. On Monday, Arizona fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, but that won't fix the lack of playmakers in its secondary.

Williams could be in line for another big game before the Commanders add to their wide receiver corps.

WR Tai Felton vs. Atlanta Falcons (Less Than 1 Percent Rostered)

Here's a super sleeper who's far under the radar, rostered in less than one percent of leagues. Since the Minnesota Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders, Tai Felton has carved out a role in the passing game.

In Cousins' two starts, Felton has nine catches for 75 yards. Last week, against the San Francisco 49ers, the second-year wideout saw a team-high 12 targets.

The Vikings haven't placed wide receiver Jordan Addison on injured reserve, but as long as he's out with a thumb injury, Felton should be rostered. This week, he could be a high-end WR2 in a favorable matchup with the Atlanta Falcons' 30th-ranked pass defense.

Furthermore, the Falcons have allowed at least three passing touchdowns in each of their last two games and are tied for seventh in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers. Opposing teams are shredding their pass coverage.

TE Tyler Higbee vs. Green Bay Packers (19 Percent Rostered)

Until Davante Adams returns from hamstring surgery, quarterback Matthew Stafford will rely on an unproven wide receiver unit and a trio of tight ends in the passing game.

Among Stafford's available pass-catchers, Tyler Higbee draws the most intrigue despite a tough tight-end matchup.

The Green Bay Packers are allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to tight ends, but Higbee doesn't take all of his snaps as an inline tight end. He also lines up in the slot and may even see targets out wide given the Rams' wide receiver injuries.

In a Week 10 blowout win over the Arizona Cardinals, Higbee saw more targets than fellow tight ends Colby Parkinson (two) and Davis Allen (one). He caught three passes for 17 yards and a touchdown, but his receiving volume could rise in a more competitive game against Green Bay.

TE Mason Taylor at Miami Dolphins (7 Percent Rostered)

Mason Taylor is the other half of this week's sleeper stack. In the New York Jets' first meeting with the Miami Dolphins, Geno Smith connected with him six times for 62 yards and two touchdowns.

Though Taylor is unlikely to log another two-touchdown performance against the Dolphins, he's primed for a big role and faces a defense that ranks eighth in fantasy points allowed to tight ends.

For now, Taylor has a bigger role than rookie first-rounder Kenyon Sadiq at tight end. The former has played 63 percent of the offensive snaps, compared to the latter's 44 percent .

In a plus matchup against a familiar opponent, Taylor has TE1 upside.

Fantasy points scored against statistics are provided by FantasyPros .

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: B/R's Week 12 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: Thanksgiving Week is a big one for both the NFL and fantasy football managers.
articles.body:
Thanksgiving Week is a big one for both the NFL and fantasy football managers.

For the NFL, it's a chance to dominate the sports conversation that much more. Starting with Wednesday's game in Los Angeles, there will be football played on five of six nights.

That's something of a hassle in fantasy—the entire week's timetable gets thrown into a blender. But it also means no teams get an off week, so the trade-off for that jumbled calendar is having a full complement of players at their disposal.

Many can use all the help they can get. With just a few weeks remaining in the regular season, teams hovering just above or just below .500 can't afford to come out on the short end in Week 12. If they want to make the playoffs, they need a win.

To help fantasy managers make their Week 12 lineup decisions, we've compiled position-by-position PPR rankings, player notes, start-or-sit recommendations and sleepers.

Before we get to the sortable, searchable player rankings for PPR leagues in Week 12, here are the always-popular notes.

The first is the same as always: While the overall player rankings can aid fantasy managers in making "flex" lineup decisions, they do not include quarterbacks. If your league features a "superflex" spot and you have depth at quarterback, flexing your QB2 is a good idea.

With games on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday and Monday this week, no teams have Week 12 off. All 32 NFL clubs are in action.

Finally, many fantasy managers have little margin for error at this point in the season. If you're facing an uphill battle in your matchup, don't be afraid to prioritize upside over a safer floor.

Use these rankings as a guide, but trust your judgment when making close lineup decisions.

* Arizona Cardinals' QBs are unranked due to the lack of a named starter at this time.

For a big chunk of this season, it has been a two-man race to be the No. 1 fantasy quarterback between Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills and Joe Burrow of the Cincinnati Bengals.

But now an NFC signal-caller is trying to crash the party.

After lighting up the Tennessee Titans for 325 yards and four touchdowns last week, Dak Prescott of the Dallas Cowboys has moved past Allen and into second place among all quarterbacks in fantasy points . Prescott has topped 300 passing yards in three straight games and has 11 touchdown passes over that span.

Given the defensive deficiencies in Dallas, the Cowboys are going to need to win shootouts to make the playoffs.

And Prescott has a real chance to catch Burrow for fantasy's top spot under center.

There has been no shortage of injuries at the quarterback position this year, and we saw another signal-caller get banged up in Week 11.

Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert's difficult season continued last week, when he entered the NFL's concussion protocol.

If Herbert sits this week, 10 NFL teams will have a different starting quarterback in Week 12 than they did in the season opener: the Arizona Cardinals, Baltimore Ravens, Indianapolis Colts, Las Vegas Raiders, Los Angeles Chargers, Miami Dolphins, Minnesota Vikings, New England Patriots, New York Giants and Philadelphia Eagles.

San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has come a long way since being selected with the final pick of the 2022 draft. Entering Week 12, he is a legitimate MVP candidate, leads the league in yards per attempt and ranks third among quarterbacks in fantasy points per game.

Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars (vs. Tennessee Titans)

Lawrence struggled last week against the New York Giants, and he has one touchdown pass in two of his last three starts. But the Tennessee Titans are a prime "get right" spot—since the Titans dealt defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and safety Amani Hooker, the Tennessee defense has been non-existent.

Matthew Stafford, Los Angeles Rams (vs. Green Bay Packers)

Given that Stafford has been playing without his top two wide receivers, his performance against the Cardinals last week—249 passing yards and three touchdowns—was a solid effort. Equaling it this week won't be easy, though. The Packers have allowed the fifth-fewest fantasy points per game to quarterbacks in 2026.

Deshaun Watson, Cleveland Browns (vs. Las Vegas Raiders)

Watson hasn't done a lot where passing touchdowns are concerned—his last one came all the way back on October 11. But Watson has thrown for over 300 yards in each of his last three games, he has a rushing score in two of those games and the Raiders have given up the fifth-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks.

The top-five fantasy running backs after 11 weeks are mostly the usual suspects—Jahmyr Gibbs of the Detroit Lions, Christian McCaffrey of the San Francisco 49ers and Bijan Robinson of the Atlanta Falcons were all first-round picks on average.

But Chuba Hubbard of the Carolina Panthers sitting third in PPR points at this point in the year is a surprise.

Hubbard currently sits eighth in the league in rushing with 831 yards and fourth in the NFL in rushing scores with nine. At his current pace, Hubbard would top 1,400 yards on the ground, which would be a career-high and then some.

Add in 31 catches and two more scores as a receiver, and you have a top-five fantasy asset who came with a low-end RB3 price tag on average in drafts last summer.

There are a pair of fantasy-relevant running backs playing early in Week 12 who are nursing injuries. Kenneth Walker III of the Kansas City Chiefs (groin) and Kyren Williams (toe) of the Los Angeles Rams both missed practice time this week. Williams is off the injury report and expected to play, but Walker is questionable after missing the last two games.

It has been a rocky second season for Ashton Jeanty of the Las Vegas Raiders—Jeanty is averaging just 3.4 yards per carry and was demoted for a short time. But after logging 169 total yards and a score against the Broncos last week, Jeanty has cracked the top 10 at his position in PPR points, and no player in the NFL has more yards after the catch in 2026.

Rookie running back Jonah Coleman of the Denver Broncos has had quite the coming-out party since assuming the lead role in the backfield, and last week Coleman went ballistic against the Raiders. Coleman carried the ball 24 times for 111 yards, found the end zone three times and finished Week 11 as fantasy's highest-scoring running back.

Quinshon Judkins, Cleveland Browns (vs. Las Vegas Raiders)

Judkins and the Cleveland ground game have struggled to get going this season—the Browns are 24th in the league in rushing at 97.5 yards per game. But the Raiders have struggled defending the run this season—Vegas has the worst run defense in the AFC, allowing just under 150 yards per game.

Tony Pollard, Tennessee Titans (at Jacksonville Jaguars)

Pollard has been solid this season—he ranks inside the top-20 running backs in PPR points and is on pace to record his fifth straight 1,000-yard season. But the Jaguars have been tough to run on dating back to last season, and Jacksonville is giving up the fewest PPR points per game in the AFC to running backs.

Samaje Perine, Cincinnati Bengals (vs. New Orleans Saints)

Monday night against the Washington Commanders, Perine had just one fewer touch than Chase Brown and out-gained Brown 97-36. It's not the first time this season that Perine has been the more effective back for the Bengals, and Sunday he faces a Saints team surrendering the third-most PPR points per game to running backs this year.

The quest to be fantasy football's No. 1 wide receiver in 2026 appears to be turning into a two-man race.

In Lane No. 1 we have Jaxon Smith-Njigba of the Seattle Seahawks, who has been robotically productive this season. Last week's bye was the first time Smith-Njigba has slowed down all season—he's averaging over 120 receiving yards per game, leads the league in touchdown catches and hasn't had less than 12 PPR points in a game this season.

In lane No. 2, we have CeeDee Lamb of the Dallas Cowboys. He hasn't quite matched Smith-Njigba's per-game numbers, and Dallas has not yet had its bye week. But the seventh-year veteran is the only other wideout in the league who has averaged 100 yards a game this season.

If you rostered either this season, WR1 is one spot you don't have to worry about.

It has been a wildly disappointing season for Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf, and last week against the Philadelphia Eagles, that season hit a new low when he was ejected after receiving two personal-foul penalties involving Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean.

Metcalf denied trying to poke DeJean in the eye and reportedly won't be suspended, but he's next to impossible for fantasy managers to trust at this point.

Metcalf is far from the only wideout who has been a letdown this year. As a rookie, Emeka Egbuka of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers had 20 catches of 20 or more yards, and three receptions of 40 or more yards. This year Egbuka has three catches of 20 or more yards, and no grabs of 40 or more yards. His last game with 65 receiving yards came over a year ago.

After a midseason slump that included a missed game, George Pickens of the Dallas Cowboys has been on a rip of late. Over the last two games, Pickens has 18 catches for 247 yards and four touchdowns. Pickens is fantasy's highest-scoring wide receiver over that span—ahead of his teammate CeeDee Lamb.

Jakobi Meyers, Jacksonville Jaguars (vs. Tennessee Titans)

Parker Washington is a clear fantasy starter, but Meyers also deserves consideration in Week 12. The Titans offer a favorable matchup, allowing the most PPR points per game to opposing receivers by a wide margin.

Mike Evans, San Francisco 49ers (vs. Seattle Seahawks)

After missing time with a sore Achilles, Evans returned with a bang last week against the Minnesota Vikings—six catches for 109 yards and a touchdown. Evans carries more than a little risk in Week 12 though—the Seahawks mark the second straight bottom-five fantasy matchup for his position that Evans has drawn.

Ryan Flournoy, Dallas Cowboys (vs. Philadelphia Eagles)

Flournoy is coming off a down week—just one catch for 11 yards in last week's win over the Titans. But the No. 3 wide receiver for the Cowboys is a top-30 fantasy option in his own right ahead of a Thanksgiving matchup with an Eagles team giving up the third-most PPR points per game to wide receivers in 2026.

When all is said and done, Travis Kelce of the Kansas City Chiefs will go down as one of the best tight ends ever to play the game. And in last week's blowout win over the Arizona Cardinals, he made some more history.

The 37-year-old caught six passes for 74 yards and a pair of touchdowns against the Redbirds, giving him 109 career touchdowns including the postseason. That moved Kelce past Rob Gronkowski and into third place among tight ends, trailing only Tony Gonzalez and Antonio Gates.

Kelce is having his best season in years—his 58.6 receiving yards per game are his most since the 2023 season, and right now he is averaging a career-best 14.3 yards per reception.

Kelce ranks among the top-five tight ends in PPR points for the season, alongside a who's who of the position in Brock Bowers of the Raiders, Trey McBride of the Cardinals and George Kittle of the 49ers. But there is a surprise of sorts among the elite fantasy options at the position—after 11 weeks only McBride has more PPR points than Isaiah Likely of the New York Giants.

McBride's season has been impressive—he's one off CeeDee Lamb's pace in receptions with 87, and his 689 yards also lead all tight ends. What's even more impressive is that McBride has just one outing with less than 10 PPR points this year despite playing with four different quarterbacks.

It has been an up-and-down ride, but after 11 weeks Harold Fannin Jr. of the Cleveland Browns ranks right about where he was drafted last summer—sixth in PPR points among tight ends. He's been that much better of late—Fannin has at least 13 PPR points in his last four games and ranks third in PPR points per game over that span.

Chigoziem Okonkwo, Washington Commanders (at Arizona Cardinals)

With wide receiver Terry McLaurin out for the season, Okonkwo has upped his game—he's sixth among tight ends in PPR points over the last three weeks after four catches for 66 yards against the Bengals last week. Now he faces an Arizona Cardinals team giving up the fourth-most PPR points per game to tight ends this year.

Kyle Pitts, Atlanta Falcons (at Minnesota Vikings)

Pitts has been all over the place this year, and after finishing second in PPR points at the position last year Pitts sits outside the top-20 so far this season. That's not likely to change this week in the Twin Cities—no team is giving up fewer PPR points per game to tight ends this season.

Pat Freiermuth, Pittsburgh Steelers (vs. Denver Broncos)

The Steelers have struggled offensively over the past couple of weeks, but Freiermuth has quietly been a top-five fantasy tight end over that admittedly brief span. Now Freiermuth and the Steelers host a Broncos team on Black Friday that has surrendered the third-most PPR points per game to tight ends in 2026.

Week 11 was not a good one for high-end fantasy defenses.

Entering last week, no team defense had more fantasy points than the Minnesota Vikings. But Brian Flores' ultra-aggressive unit was overwhelmed in Mexico City, where Minnesota managed just one sack and no takeaways in a 35-10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

It wasn't a stunner in a terrible matchup, but it still stung.

Things didn't go much better for the team that entered the week second in fantasy points. Like the Vikings, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers had an unfavorable matchup in Week 11 in Detroit against the Lions. And like the Vikings, they faceplanted—a single sack and 31 points allowed.

The Chicago Bears are better known for their offense than their defense, but that defense has played a part in the team winning eight of its first 10 games.

Last week against the floundering Saints, Chicago logged six sacks, two takeaways and a safety on the way to the best fantasy performance of Week 11.

The Houston Texans have spent most of the 2026 campaign disappointing fantasy managers—the team was drafted as a high-end weekly starter but had performed like a so-so matchup play. But after two sacks, a takeaway and a safety last week against the Colts, the Texans are third in points since their bye week.

After Tyler Bass missed from 54 yards out last week against the Miami Dolphins, there is now just one kicker in the NFL who has attempted 20 field goals this season without a miss. That kicker is Chase McLaughlin of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who has attempted at least 20 field goals this season without a miss.

The Giants have been inconsistent defensively over most of this season, but Big Blue is sixth among defenses in fantasy points over the last three weeks ahead of a trip to face an imploding Colts team.

Wil Lutz, Denver Broncos (at Pittsburgh Steelers)

Lutz hasn't been especially productive this season, but that should change against the Steelers, who have surrendered the second-most fantasy points to kickers this season.

The Bills have availed themselves of a string of favorable matchups over the last month—no defense has more fantasy points over that span. But the Chiefs are the exact opposite of a favorable matchup, and Allen vs. Mahomes tends to turn into a shootout.

Cairo Santos, Chicago Bears (at Detroit Lions)

Santos' 81 percent field-goal conversion rate and K15 ranking limit his appeal. Facing a Lions team that has given up the fewest fantasy points per game to kickers is worse.

The Jets have spent most of this season off the fantasy radar, ranking outside the top-20 defenses for the season. But this week's matchup is appealing—the Dolphins have given up the fifth-most fantasy points per game to defenses this year.

Dominic Zvada, New York Giants (at Indianapolis Colts)

Zvada is tied for third in the league with 27 field-goal attempts this year. Although seven misses have limited his fantasy production, his high attempt volume makes him worth considering in Week 12 at Indianapolis.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

Week 12 is going to be a fun one. It will open with a potential playoff preview between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams. While Los Angeles has lost wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, it still has a fearsome pass rush led by Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett, and Byron Young. That could be a massive problem for a Packers offensive line that has been average at absolute best.

The Detroit Lions will host the rival Chicago Bears early Thursday afternoon. It'll be a serious test for a Detroit defense that has lost star pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a season-ending knee injury.

The Dallas Cowboys will host the Philadelphia Eagles in the late afternoon game. Dallas has an atrocious defense, but a better offense and a healthier overall roster could allow the Cowboys to escape with another win.

Thursday night's matchup could be the highlight of the week. Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes always create high drama when they get together. However, the weather conditions could favor the team with the better defense. That's been Kansas City this season.

Friday's matchup has become a must-win for the Pittsburgh Steelers. They led the AFC North not too long ago and are now fading in the wild-card race. If Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos can play better on the road than they have of late, they can really hurt Pittsburgh's playoff chances.

Sunday's slate will feature some terrific games, too. The showdown between the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers could essentially hand San Francisco the NFC West with a win. Of course, the 49ers narrowly escaped in the first meeting, and Sam Darnold appears on track to return for Seattle.

Whether Darnold is actually an upgrade over backup Drew Lock is another matter.

No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza will look to get his first win against a Browns team that has a habit of letting games come down to the final moments.

Monday's finale could be a last stand of sorts for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. They hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Carolina Panthers right now. However, the Bucs have also lost two straight and are sitting at 3-7. They'll need to get their ground game back on track if they hope to make up ground in the NFC South.

articles.title: The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph to start at QB vs Broncos
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers’ long, accomplished career took a stunning twist in his final season.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers’ long, accomplished career took a stunning twist in his final season. The four-time NFL MVP has been benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers and Mason Rudolph will start against the Denver Broncos on Friday. Rodgers will be inactive for the game, the team said in a statement late Tuesday night. Rodgers, who turns 43 next week, has completed 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards with 16 touchdown passes and six interceptions. The Steelers (6-4) have lost two in a row and Rodgers struggled in both games, though the receiving corps has been depleted. Rudolph has started just 19 games in seven seasons with the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, going 9-9-1. He went 3-0 down the stretch in 2023 while filling in for Kenny Pickett and led Pittsburgh to the playoffs. The Steelers lost a wild-card playoff game to Buffalo that season. Rodgers returned for his 22nd season in the NFL to reunite with coach Mike McCarthy, who replaced Mike Tomlin. Rodgers and McCarthy won a Super Bowl together in Green Bay following the 2010 season. On Monday, McCarthy said Rodgers is the starter while allowing that Pittsburgh’s offense needs a jolt after back-to-back losses to Cincinnati and Philadelphia. “I think there’s things offensively we need to do better and that always benefits and leads in the quarterback play,” McCarthy said Monday. “So, I just need him to just keep plowing away.” That changed a day later. Rodgers wasn’t listed on the team’s injury report and spoke to reporters after practice, acknowledging only that “you’ve got to be playing your best ball this time of year, so we’ve got to bounce back accordingly this week.” The Steelers are scheduled to practice on Wednesday afternoon ahead of a visit by the surging Broncos on Black Friday. It’s a shocking move by the Steelers considering Rodgers’ relationship with McCarthy – he played a role in his hiring – and the alternative. Rodgers has an 86.6 passer rating, which is the lowest in his career. Rudolph is a career backup with a passer rating of 84.3. McCarthy even stressed Tuesday that he and Rodgers met that morning as usual, noting that “there’s really not a spot he hasn’t been in,” during his Hall of Fame-caliber career. Maybe, but this is a new one. But the Steelers are looking for someone to spark an offense that’s 23rd in total yards (310.4 per game), 22nd in passing (198.6) and is averaging 21.4 points. Pittsburgh is tied with Cleveland and currently holds a wild-card spot in the AFC with a one-game lead over New England (5-5). Rodgers has been sacked 31 times this season, including five times in a 19-16 loss at Philadelphia on Sunday. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 227 yards and one TD with no picks. Rodgers actually led the team in rushing with 29 yards, including a 12-yard scamper. Wide receiver DK Metcalf had just one catch on four targets before he was ejected from the game. Veteran wideout Michael Pittman Jr. didn’t play. Pittsburgh’s leading receiver against the Eagles was Max Hurleman, a guy making his NFL debut. It’s uncertain whether Rodgers will ask for his release so he can have an opportunity to join another team to close out his career. Daniel Jones also is a free agent after he was released last week by the Indianapolis Colts. Rodgers led the Steelers to a 10-6 record last season in his first year with the team. They lost 30-6 to Houston in a wild-card game. Rodgers ranks third on the NFL’s all-time list with 543 touchdown passes, fifth in passing yards at 68,515 and fifth with 5,916 complete passes. His 101.6 passer rating is fourth-best.

articles.title: New Aaron Rodgers Rumors on Fallout From Steelers QB's Shocking Benching for Mason Rudolph
articles.summary: ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter provided some context Wednesday regarding what went into the Pittsburgh Steelers' decision to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter provided some context Wednesday regarding what went into the Pittsburgh Steelers' decision to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos.

According to Schefter, the Steelers held multiple meetings Tuesday with a source describing them as "some good, some bad." At the conclusion of the meetings, the Steelers decided to name Rudolph the starter for their Week 12 game.

Rodgers, who is not in the Steelers' building on Wednesday, was "excused" from team activities "while he processes" the team's decision, Schefter reported.

Rodgers Claims McCarthy Fell Asleep in Meetings

NFL insider Jordan Schultz added the relationship between Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy "has not been in a good place" and it's "unlikely" they can reconcile.

"The frustration is not just with Rodgers," Schultz reported. "Multiple position groups have been upset, and I'm told McCarthy has not been what some offensive players hoped for. Frustration has been growing among everyone for weeks."

Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported that it "seems a release is destined to happen."

The Steelers made the surprising announcement Tuesday night, releasing a statement in which they revealed that Rodgers will be inactive for Friday's contest:

Per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo, the Steelers had been planning to change their offensive play-calling process, as Rodgers asked for quarterback Tom Arth to be the one relaying the play calls to him:

However, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, McCarthy ultimately made the call to bench Rodgers instead, believing Rudolph gives the team the best chance to win:

While Rodgers has helped lead the Steelers to a 6-4 start this season, the team has dropped back-to-back games in disappointing fashion.

Following a 38-18 road loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, the Steelers fell 19-16 this past weekend to a Philadelphia Eagles team starting third-string quarterback Joe Milton.

While Rodgers threw a combined three touchdown passes and no interceptions over those two defeats, the Pittsburgh offense looked listless as a whole, averaging just 17 points and 238.5 yards of total offense.

Rodgers, who turns 43 on Dec. 2, is one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history, as evidenced by his 10 career Pro Bowl nods, four First Team All-Pro selections, four NFL MVP awards and one Super Bowl win and Super Bowl MVP Award.

His numbers have slipped in recent years, although he did throw 24 touchdowns compared to seven interceptions, while leading the Steelers to the playoffs last season.

Given that result, the Steelers decided to bring Rodgers back for the 2026 campaign, and Rodgers announced prior to the start of the season that it would be his final one before retirement.

Overall, Rodgers is completing 60.9 percent of his passes for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions this season, and he has had some stretches where he has played legitimately good football.

Most notably, he had three consecutive games with three touchdown passes, and he has also led Pittsburgh to wins over fellow current playoff teams in the Bengals and Cleveland Browns.

Despite the Steelers' offensive struggles in recent weeks, the decision to bench Rodgers is a controversial one given that Pittsburgh has a one-game lead over the New England Patriots for an AFC wild-card spot.

Also, it is now possible that Rodgers has played the final snap of his NFL career should McCarthy and the Steelers decide to stick with Rudolph the rest of the way with Will Howard and Drew Allar as backup options.

Of course, the Steelers could potentially release Rodgers and give him a chance to catch on elsewhere for the remainder of this season, but it is unclear if Pittsburgh has considered that option.

articles.title: “You can’t hold on to the ball”: Fernando Mendoza gets honest feedback from Las Vegas Raiders legend ahead of Cleveland Browns matchup
articles.summary: Three touchdown passes should earn a rookie quarterback some praise. For Fernando Mendoza, they came with a warning label.
articles.body: Three touchdown passes should earn a rookie quarterback some praise. For Fernando Mendoza, they came with a warning label. The Las Vegas Raiders passer threw for 267 yards in a 38-24 loss to the Denver Broncos on Nov. 22, but he also took five sacks. The Raiders fell to 4-7. Now the Cleveland Browns await in a Week 12 primetime game. Former Raiders offensive lineman Lincoln Kennedy has a clear message for the number one overall pick: throw the ball sooner.Fernando Mendoza sack problem and Lincoln Kennedy’s blunt adviceMendoza completed 18 of 37 passes with one interception and posted an 88.5 passer rating. The stat line looks healthy. The sack count tells a different story. Kennedy spent his career in the trenches, so he knows how a slow release feels from the line's side.He broke it down on the recent episode of "The Raiders Squad Show."“His vision, his overall vision,” Kennedy said on the episode of “The Raiders Squad Show.” “I think what needs to be sort of fine-tuned is his timing. He has to understand you can’t hold on to the ball. Even if you extend a play with your legs, you’ve got to get rid of the ball. You can’t wait for anyone to come open.”He further added, “You have to anticipate him. You might even have to direct them. If you’re pointing downfield, go this way because I’m going to throw it there. He’s got accuracy, which aids him, but he still holds on to the ball far too long. His awareness from one week to the next has grown. He’s gotten better, but he still holds on to the ball far too long.”Raiders vs. Browns: What Fernando Mendoza can build onThe criticism comes with real respect for the player. Kennedy sees growth from Mendoza's first start to his second, and Denver saw it too. Prime Video insider James Palmer shared what the Broncos' locker room thought.“There certainly was a lot of respect for Fernando Mendoza in the Broncos locker room,” Palmer wrote on X. “What stood out was how calm he was in the pocket and his feel in the pocket, as well as how unpredictable he is when he starts to move.“Most young players have something they do and go to it over and over again. Mendoza scrambles out [in] a variety of ways and scans the field well while doing it.”That mix of poise and creativity keeps plays alive. It can also tempt a young passer to wait for something better. Against Cleveland, the plan is simple. Read the field, pick the first good option and let it go. A faster release would protect Mendoza and give his line a fairer fight.The Raiders have six games left, starting with Cleveland, and the schedule gives Mendoza a short runway to show what he can become. Wins would help, but the Raiders also want evidence. Quicker decisions, fewer sacks and steady drives would tell them far more about their rookie than the final score alone.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
