articles.title: Aaron Rodgers: Pittsburgh Steelers drop four-time MVP as starting quarterback
articles.summary: Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers may have played his last game in the NFL after being dropped by the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers may have played his last game in the NFL after being dropped by the Pittsburgh Steelers.

In a brief statement published late on Tuesday local time, the Steelers said Mason Rudolph will be their starting quarterback for Friday's home game against the Denver Broncos.

The Steelers added that Rodgers, the NFL's four-time Most Valuable Player, will be inactive for the game so will not serve as back-up to 31-year-old Rudolph.

Rodgers, who turns 43 next week, was not listed on the Steelers' injury list on Tuesday and ESPN reports , external leaving him out was a coaching decision.

The quarterback appeared on US sports TV programme the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday and confirmed his time with the Steelers was over.

He was also critical of Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, accusing him of snoring while he slept through team meetings.

McCarthy was in charge of the Green Bay Packers for most of Rodgers' 18-year spell in Wisconsin, including their Super Bowl win in 2011.

Rodgers, who joined Pittsburgh in 2025 after two years with the New York Jets , was "99% sure" he was going to retire after leading the Steelers to last season's play-offs.

However, McCarthy's appointment by Pittsburgh persuaded him to play one more year.

Although the Steelers have a 6-4 record, they have suffered two straight defeats after losing 19-16 at the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday.

When asked about a potential change on Monday, McCarthy said "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback".

But a day later the Steelers announced that is no longer the case.

Rodgers handed 'chastening demotion' - analysis

Pittsburgh's 29-word statement, , external published at 23:10 local time, could be an unceremonious end to an illustrious career.

While Rodgers was unable to claim a second Super Bowl win, he was named the season MVP in 2011, 2014, 2020 and 2021. Only Peyton Manning (five) has won the award more times.

Rodgers insisted his 22nd year in the NFL would be his last, and he has been benched at a crucial stage in the season.

The Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) lead the AFC North division, with Pittsburgh third, but with seven games left the Steelers occupy the final play-off spot for the AFC Conference.

Although Pittsburgh are 6-4, they have had to grind out some of those wins as they have struggled offensively. They rank 22nd for both points and passing yards per game.

Rodgers is undoubtedly past his best, but his form has only dropped slightly from last season and the team's struggles are by no means entirely down to him.

The Steelers' depth among their wide receivers is thin. Michael Pittman is out injured and DK Metcalf has not delivered the production expected when he was brought in with Rodgers before the 2025 season.

Metcalf, 28, was even ejected during Sunday's loss at Philadelphia, meaning Rodgers had to lean on debutant Max Hurleman with the game on the line.

And it is not as if Pittsburgh had a hot-shot rookie quarterback pushing for an opportunity to impress.

Rudolph is in his ninth season and has started each as a back-up. After being drafted by the Steelers in 2018, he joined Tennessee for the 2024 season then returned to Pittsburgh, starting 19 of his 38 career games.

McCarthy is hoping Rudolph can spark his offence, but if he doesn't, would they revert to Rodgers or try the two young quarterbacks on their roster?

It would be some U-turn for the Steelers to ask the veteran to step back in after what has to be considered a chastening demotion, a move the team knew would grab headlines.

Teams seldom make such a sudden change at this stage in the season, especially those with a winning record and a quarterback of Rodgers' stature.

Rodgers has clashed with team management, team-mates and coaches throughout his career - including McCarthy - so would he be willing to come to his aid if asked? His comments on Wednesday suggest not.

Whatever happens over the coming weeks, this is certainly not the farewell one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time was hoping for.

articles.title: Daniel Jones' Potential Landing Spots Discussed in New NFL Rumors Amid Patriots Buzz
articles.summary: Following his surprising release by the Indianapolis Colts last week, quarterback Daniel Jones reportedly could take a wait-and-see approach before choosing his next NFL destination.
articles.body:
Following his surprising release by the Indianapolis Colts last week, quarterback Daniel Jones reportedly could take a wait-and-see approach before choosing his next NFL destination.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , some league sources are wondering whether Jones might opt to be patient and see if any major injuries befell starting quarterbacks across the NFL rather than quickly catching on with another team.

Fowler named the New England Patriots as the "natural fit" for Jones given that starting quarterback Drake Maye could miss the rest of the season with a fractured fibula.

On top of that, the Pats are still very much in the playoff race at 5-5, as they trail the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns by only one game for a wild-card spot in the AFC.

However, Fowler noted that Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel "seems intent" on starting Tommy DeVito at quarterback for this week at the very least, and ESPN's Dan Graziano added that he too believes the Patriots "want to go with" DeVito.

Both Fowler and Graziano acknowledged the possibility of New England exploring other options if DeVito performs poorly against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, though.

Jones, 29, was well on his way to the best season of his career in 2025 before a torn Achilles cut his campaign short after 13 games.

He had posted an 8-5 record as a starter and was completing 68.0 percent of his passes for 3,101 yards, 19 touchdowns and eight interceptions, while also rushing for five scores.

Jones' quality play did not carry over to this season, though, as he went 3-8 and completed 58.4 percent of his passing attempts for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns and a league-high 13 interceptions prior to his release.

Given his form and the idea that Jones may not be back to normal physically until next season because of the long road to recovery after an Achilles tear, both Fowler and Graziano questioned whether there is much of anything Jones can do this season to rebuild his value heading into free agency this coming offseason.

While Jones has his warts after how he performed in Indianapolis this season, he could still prove to be a viable option for New England or another playoff contending team in need of a quarterback depending on how the next week or two play out.

articles.title: The Thanksgiving NFL feast gets started a day early. Here’s what you need to know
articles.summary: The NFL is serving up an extra helping of football this Thanksgiving, with its first Thanksgiving Eve game kicking off a holiday weekend packed with marquee matchups and major playoff implications.
articles.body: The NFL is serving up an extra helping of football this Thanksgiving, with its first Thanksgiving Eve game kicking off a holiday weekend packed with marquee matchups and major playoff implications. From the latest chapter of the Patrick Mahomes-Josh Allen rivalry to a heavyweight NFC North showdown, here are five things to watch in Week 12 of the NFL season. Thanksgiving Eve: A new NFL tradition Apparently, three games on Thanksgiving and another on Black Friday weren’t enough for the NFL. For the first time, the league will stage a Thanksgiving Eve game, with the Los Angeles Rams hosting the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. The matchup is part of Netflix’s five-game package this season. The streaming giant kicked off the NFL season in Australia and will also broadcast two Christmas Day games – the Packers at the Chicago Bears and the Buffalo Bills at the Denver Broncos – before wrapping up its slate on January 9. Netflix is pulling out all the stops for its Thanksgiving Eve debut, with legendary rock band U2 set to deliver a halftime performance worthy of a Super Bowl. But there are plenty of compelling storylines on the field as well. Packers star pass rusher Micah Parsons is expected to make his season debut after recovering from ACL surgery, giving Green Bay a potentially massive boost heading into the stretch run. And will Sean McVay ever figure out how to beat Matt LaFleur? The Rams head coach is 0-5 against his former assistant, a remarkable blemish on the résumé of one of the NFL’s most successful coaches. Mahomes vs. Allen: Episode XI Don’t eat so much turkey that you fall asleep early on Thursday, because the Thanksgiving nightcap is an absolute blockbuster. Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen will square off for the 11th time in what has become the defining quarterback rivalry of this generation. Through their first 10 meetings, the two superstars are dead even at 5-5. But how they’ve arrived at that record tells the story of their rivalry. Allen has largely owned the regular season, going 5-1 against Mahomes. But when the stakes have been highest, Mahomes has had the upper hand, going 4-0 against Allen in the playoffs. Both teams are rolling heading into Thursday’s showdown, with Allen’s Buffalo Bills sitting at 9-1 and Mahomes’ Kansas City Chiefs at 8-2. Incredibly, this will be just the second time in NFL history that two teams have met while each riding a three-game winning streak in which every victory came by at least 17 points. The only other instance came in 2007, when two other legendary quarterbacks were under center. Tom Brady and the 8-0 New England Patriots squared off against Peyton Manning and the 7-0 Indianapolis Colts. Nearly two decades later, Mahomes and Allen are giving football fans another rivalry for the ages. Kickoff in the Buffalo suburb of Orchard Park, New York, is set for 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. A Thanksgiving showdown for NFC North supremacy Football fans have had to endure their fair share of forgettable Detroit Lions games to kick off Thanksgiving over the years. That certainly won’t be the case Thursday. The 8-2 Lions will host the 8-2 Chicago Bears in a heavyweight showdown that could go a long way toward determining who wins the ultra-competitive NFC North. Despite dealing with numerous injuries on defense, Detroit has rattled off six consecutive victories. Chicago, meanwhile, has won five straight. The Bears have actually been unbeatable when Caleb Williams has been able to go the distance. Chicago has yet to lose a game this season that its franchise quarterback has both started and finished. Williams’ emergence has helped transform the Bears into legitimate contenders, and Thursday presents another opportunity to prove they belong among the NFC’s elite. Oddsmakers are expecting fireworks, too. The game’s over/under of 55.5 points is the highest of any matchup in Week 12. Browns and Raiders in primetime? Believe it. Here’s a sentence virtually no one would have expected to read before the season began: The Cleveland Browns and Las Vegas Raiders have been flexed into Sunday Night Football. That’s right. The NFL is moving the Browns-Raiders matchup from the Sunday afternoon slate into primetime, replacing the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Chargers. And rightfully so. The Browns have been one of the biggest surprises of the NFL season. At 6-4, Cleveland would be in the playoffs if the postseason started today. Meanwhile, with No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza now under center for the Raiders, there’s plenty of intrigue surrounding the young quarterback and how he’ll develop as the face of the franchise. Browns fans certainly have been getting their money’s worth this season, particularly those attending games in Cleveland. Deshaun Watson has engineered a fourth-quarter comeback in every single Browns victory this season, making late-game drama a weekly occurrence. Cleveland is also 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963. It’s been a remarkable turnaround for a franchise that entered the season with few expectations. And now, the Browns will get an opportunity to showcase their resurgence in front of a national television audience. Brock Purdy’s MVP push The Seattle Seahawks will be the next team tasked with trying to slow down Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers’ top-ranked offense on Sunday afternoon. Good luck. Regardless of who is available at wide receiver, Purdy continues to put up spectacular numbers. The former Mr. Irrelevant just carved up the NFL’s top-ranked defense, throwing for 255 yards and three touchdowns against the Minnesota Vikings. Through 10 games, Purdy has thrown 23 touchdown passes against just five interceptions and leads the NFL in both Total QBR and passer rating. Oddsmakers currently have Purdy trailing only Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow in the race for the league’s Most Valuable Player award. For much of his career, the debate surrounding Purdy has centered on how much of his success can be attributed to Kyle Shanahan’s offensive system and the talented supporting cast around him. But given the revolving door of personnel at receiver and his continued excellence, that argument is becoming increasingly difficult to make. If Purdy keeps producing at this level and the 49ers hold on to the NFC’s best record and secure the No. 1 seed in the playoffs, it’s going to be awfully difficult to deny him the MVP award. articles.title: Ahead of Micah Parsons' return for Packers-Rams, Aaron Donald jokes: 'Micah, if you want to take one more week …'
articles.summary: Each team is aware of its closing postseason window. And each team is aware that the playoff formula gives no grace on account of injuries — particularly in...
articles.body:
Three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald said what the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams might all be thinking: "I wish he would stay out one more week."

Donald was referring to Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons. A member of the Packers might also have applied the sentiment to Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett.

Instead, the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game will feature a matchup of two teams who spent big to upgrade their pass rush recently — before injuries sunk their hopes within months.

The Packers dealt their 2026 and 2027 first-round picks as well as defensive tackle Kenny Clark to the Dallas Cowboys in August 2025 in exchange for Parsons. He raced to 12.5 sacks last year as the Packers were 9-3-1 before Parsons tore his ACL and meniscus last Dec. 14.

After 11 months, the Packers activated him this week with the expectation he'll debut Wednesday in first-year defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon's defense.

Allow Donald, who emerged from a two-year retirement Aug. 30 to rejoin the Rams, to wish that Parsons would wait another week.

"A fan of Micah, I think he's one hell of a football player, fast, explosive, plays with an unbelievable motor," Donald told reporters on Sunday. "If he does play this week, that's going to be huge for them. Micah, if you want to take one more week to get yourself 100%, make sure everything is where it needs to be, I'd like to see you on TV.

"I know they're going to be happy to have him back."

To the Packers' dismay, Garrett is back in the mix as well.

The reigning Defensive Player of the Year missed seven games this season when swelling in his knee dictated in-season surgery. The injury was a major blow after the Rams traded edge rusher Jared Verse alongside their 2027 first-, 2028 second- and 2029 third-round picks to acquire Garrett on June 1. The Rams won the Super Bowl last time it was at their home base, SoFi Stadium. Their all-in actions chased a repeat this season as the game returns to SoFi, and as 38-year-old quarterback Matthew Stafford's career nears its twilight.

Garrett returned Nov. 8 against the Washington Commanders to the tune of three sacks and six pressures. He registered another pressure in 17 snaps the following week against the Arizona Cardinals.

Expect Packers quarterback Jordan Love to be his next target.

"We played Myles last year, we know what he's about," Love told reporters. "He's a speed guy. He's got power though as well. So he's a great edge rusher, but you got to have a plan. Obviously we're on the road, so crowd noise will be a little bit of a factor. But you got to be able to be dialed into the snap count and get off on time.

"Because if you miss a step, Myles is the guy that will be right around you."

Why Rams might have more answers to Parsons than Packers do for Garrett

Garrett and Parsons are not identical players. Each levies a quick get-off to frustrate opposing offensive linemen, but at 6-foot-4 and 272 pounds, Garrett imposes with size beyond Parsons' 6-3, 250-pound frame.

Each player has flashed against the pass and run. But pass rushing is both players' specialty. One of the NFL's go-to counters for pass rushers of Garrett and Parsons' multi-year All-Pro ilk: establishing the run to keep defenders honest.

That recipe looks far more promising for one team Wednesday than the other.

While the Rams will hurt from the absence of receivers Puka Nacua (season-ending knee surgery) and Davante Adams (hamstring surgery on Oct. 20, with a 6-10 week recovery), Los Angeles has established a diverse offensive attack that also capitalizes on tight ends and running backs.

In addition to ranking top-10 in passing yards and touchdowns, the Rams rank seventh each in rushing yards and touchdowns. When Parsons chases Stafford, the Rams should have outlets.

"Anytime you got Matthew Stafford, no matter who's out there in the field, you have a great chance to win," Parsons said. "And they got two incredible backs [in Kyren Williams and Blake Corum], they have a great tight end personnel. I mean, you're seeing a similar variation in Buffalo. They're running a lot of 12P (two tight-end personnel) with Dawson Knox and [Dalton] Kincaid with James Cook out of the backfield. So we're seeing that kind of variation across the league with guys who can fit that personnel set. And [the] Rams [have] been running a lot of 13 personnel [three tight ends]. So it really doesn't surprise me. When you have a great offensive coordinator like that and you can adjust to your system and the players you have, that's why [head coach Sean McVay] is one of the great ones.

"Regardless of who plays, we got our hands full on Wednesday."

Love deserves credit for how he's carried the Packers this year, his 2,838 passing yards ranking third in the league while his 20 passing touchdowns tie for eighth. He has elevated receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden into a formidable duo who have combined for 12 touchdowns with each accounting for more than 85 receiving yards per game. Green Bay's challenge, as Minnesota exposed in the Packers' last outing: They have no run game.

Injuries and time on the commissioner's exempt list after allegations of domestic violence have limited running back Josh Jacobs to three games, with Jacobs not expected to return yet this week. Add in a series of injuries to the Packers' offensive line, and the same Green Bay team that ranks third in passing yards (268.1 per game) ranks dead last in rushing yards per game (67) and yards per carry (3.06).

The result: Opponents know the Packers are overwhelmingly going to pass, and defenses pass-rush accordingly. Love has faced the quickest time to pressure through Week 11, at 2.41 seconds, per Next Gen Stats. He's coming off a game in which the Vikings pressured him on average after 2.33 seconds, the second-fastest mark of his career, generating pressure on 40% of his dropbacks — the most of Love's career.

Green Bay could receive offensive line reinforcements in center Sean Rhyan and right guard Kevin Zeitler, each of whom is officially questionable per their game status. But will the need to lean on the pass give Garrett and Donald similar confidence to what the Vikings flashed before the Packers' bye?

"It starts up front," Love said. "We got to handle business. We got to be able to block the front, give me some time. And in the run game, we got to be able to get hands on people, create some lanes in the run game.

"You look at their team, the front definitely stands out."

Packers-Rams matchup could prove 'difference between playoffs or Cancun'

If the regular season ended today, the 6-4 Packers would clinch the final NFC wild card while the 6-4 Rams would miss the cut by two spots (the Seattle Seahawks currently slot eighth).

The Packers' 40% chance to make the playoffs will improve to 62% if Green Bay wins on Wednesday, per The Athletic's NFL playoff simulator that integrates thousands of possible season outcomes. A loss would drop the Packers' chance to 25%, the major gap in large part due to the tiebreaker that Los Angeles would hold.

The Rams have less upside from a win on Wednesday, per The Athletic's predictor , their 34% chance improving to only 47% if they clinch win No. 7. But they have more downside: A loss to the Packers, and the Rams' chance of advancing to the postseason drops to 16%, per The Athletic. Even with a slew of injuries, that would disappoint a club that spent its offseason making a splash for Garrett, acquiring both of the Chiefs' veteran cornerbacks and reuniting with Donald all to upgrade the defense in hopes of maximizing Stafford's waning time.

Each team is aware of its closing postseason window. And each team is aware that the playoff formula gives no grace on account of injuries — particularly in a crowded NFC.

"I mean, we're in this conference where it's like you have to play perfect," Parsons said. "We don't got the ability [like in] basketball to lose by 40 one night and come win by 30 the next week. That's not in our future.

Will Parsons' return, or Garrett's continued settling into his team, move the needle?

Restrictions on snap count for Parsons in his first game back would not be surprising. But the Packers have worked him through rehabilitation drills and practices, including with pads, assessing his football skills as well as the symmetry of strength between his quads, hips and calves. Parsons' surgery team led by Dr. Neal ElAttrache also has monitored his post-operation recovery with cameras and force plates that detect strength, speed or functional deficits, ElAttrache told Yahoo Sports by text Tuesday night. The goal with these barometers: Return not only healthy but also with a reduced chance of re-injury.

Garrett, meanwhile, said he felt rusty in his return vs. the Commanders. Rams head coach Sean McVay qualified that assessment this week.

"Rusty for him, that's a loose term," McVay said. "I think it's more playing within the system, understanding his opp[ortunities] and understanding who he's rushing with. I think getting the call, applying it, seeing the offense. I think anybody would be rusty. He practiced that whole week [before his return], but before that, he didn't have the accumulation of snaps that a lot of the other guys did or that he would have had if he was healthy the whole time."

For both teams, and their ramping-back-up edge rushers, the stakes will echo Wednesday night across the very field each club hopes to revisit in February.

"Where we're at in the season, like I said, every one matters and you don't want to lose games because you're worried about the outcome," Parsons said. "At this point, we can say every game is going to be the difference between playoffs or Cancun."

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' Potential Free Agent Market Updated in New NFL Rumors After Steelers Benching
articles.summary: After veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers was benched for the Pittsburgh Steelers' game against the Denver Broncos on Friday, many are wondering if his time with the franchise will come to an end sooner than expected.
articles.body:
After veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers was benched for the Pittsburgh Steelers' game against the Denver Broncos on Friday, many are wondering if his time with the franchise will come to an end sooner than expected.

On Wednesday's episode of The Russini Report , NFL insider Dianna Russini addressed the possibility of Rodgers being released by the Steelers and his potential market if he becomes a free agent.

"And what if Rodgers were to get released? Could he sign with a contender whose starter gets hurt? From what I sense, I don't think there's gonna be a big market, but you never know," Russini said.

The Steelers announced on Tuesday that Mason Rudolph will be the starter for Friday's matchup, while Rodgers will be inactive:

Following Rodgers' benching, Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported that it "seems a release is destined to happen."

Rodgers is a week away from his 43rd birthday, and he already said that the 2026 season will likely be his last in the NFL. However, being released by the Steelers would be an unceremonious end to a Hall of Fame career, especially if he doesn't land with another team that could help him compete for another Super Bowl title in his final year.

articles.title: Cam Ward Explains Angry Reaction After Ridiculous TD Pass Late in Titans' Blowout Loss to Cowboys
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward made one of the best throws of the year with his late touchdown pass to Calvin Ridley in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, but he didn't even get to enjoy it.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward made one of the best throws of the year with his late touchdown pass to Calvin Ridley in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, but he didn't even get to enjoy it.

On Wednesday, Ward was asked about his angry reaction on the sideline after his highlight-reel throw, and he had a simple response.

Ward hasn't experienced much success since being selected with the No. 1 pick in the 2025 NFL draft, and he's never been shy about letting his frustrations be known. He went viral during his rookie season after the Titans' fourth straight loss when he assessed his team's performance by saying , "We ass."

During his appearance on Netflix's Quarterback docuseries, Ward explained why he doesn't mince words, even during hard times.

"That's how I've been my whole life," he said (via Pro Football Talk's Michael David Smith ). "That's how I was raised, to be honest. That's how I was brought up. For myself, I'm not playing my best ball that game, and when I said that, I meant it."

While his emotions may boil over at times, Ward has never crossed the line by calling out any of his teammates or coaches. The 24-year-old is still trying to navigate the best way to lead a rebuilding team, and it's understandable that all the losing has worn on him.

Ward and the Titans (1-9) will be trying to end a four-game losing streak when they meet the Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) on Sunday.

articles.title: Commanders' Updated Depth Chart After Brandon Aiyuk Contract in NFL Free Agency
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk's tumultuous NFL journey has reached its next step.
articles.body:
Brandon Aiyuk's tumultuous NFL journey has reached its next step.

Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told ESPN's Adam Schefter the wide receiver and Washington Commanders agreed to a deal for him to join their practice squad.

With Aiyuk entering the fold, here's Washington's updated offensive depth chart:

RB: Rachaad White, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Austin Ekeler

WR: Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, Van Jefferson

WR: Stefon Diggs, Luke McCaffrey, Brandon Aiyuk (practice squad)

TE: Chig Okonkwo, Ben Sinnott, John Bates, Colson Yankoff

Aiyuk was available after the San Francisco 49ers released him on Nov. 23.

Since the release happened after the trade deadline, Aiyuk was subject to waivers and became an unrestricted free agent when he wasn't claimed within 24 hours.

In the immediate aftermath of San Francisco's move, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the Washington Commanders' practice squad was seen as the "most likely" landing spot for the playmaker.

While Aiyuk called out Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels on social media during the summer, The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala reported the former college teammates were "now on good terms."

Aiyuk calling someone out on social media was nothing new, as he consistently ripped the 49ers and even advocated for Washington to sign him before his release. ESPN's Nick Wagoner called Aiyuk and San Francisco "a confounding partnership" when reporting on the release and wrote the relationship "began to deteriorate when the sides started negotiating a contract extension in 2024."

The two sides eventually agreed on a four-year, $120 million extension following a stalemate, although he suffered a significant knee injury during the 2024 campaign after he signed the contract.

The injury sidelined him for the rest of that season, and he didn't play in 2025 either.

Wagoner noted the 49ers eventually voided approximately $27 million in guarantees on that contract after "he didn't show up for multiple in-house rehab sessions." What's more, the receiver stopped reporting to the team's facility and stopped communicating with its leadership.

San Francisco ultimately put him on the reserve/left team list, and he didn't report to the team for its offseason program or training camp. General manager John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan also made it publicly clear Aiyuk wouldn't return even after he was reinstated.

There are now plenty of question marks surrounding Aiyuk as he heads to a new club given how his tenure with the 49ers ended. What's more, he hasn't even played in an NFL game since 2024 and suffered a serious injury the last time he was on the field for a regular-season contest.

However, he is also still just 28 years old and was one of the best receivers in the league in 2023 when he posted 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns. That was the second of back-to-back years with more than 1,000 receiving yards, and he also helped lead the 49ers to the Super Bowl during that season.

Ideally for the Commanders, he will be motivated and return to that form following this addition.

Given how public Aiyuk was in his desire to play for the Commanders, perhaps motivation will not be a concern. He also has experience playing alongside Daniels from their time together at Arizona State in 2019, so there should be some chemistry already in place.

Washington could also use more production at wide receiver with Terry McLaurin sidelined for the rest of the season with an injury, and Aiyuk returning to his previous form would provide it with just that.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers blasts Steelers coach Mike McCarthy after being benched: ‘You’re unhealthy’
articles.summary: Recently benched Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers described his head coach Mike McCarthy as “unhealthy” in a critical interview following the Steelers’ decision to deactivate Rodgers for the team’s upcoming game.
articles.body: Recently benched Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers described his head coach Mike McCarthy as “unhealthy” in a critical interview following the Steelers’ decision to deactivate Rodgers for the team’s upcoming game. Speaking to ESPN’s Pat McAfee on Wednesday, Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep during team meetings and missing walkthroughs in the weeks leading up this benching. “Last Thursday, I was in a quarterback meeting and in 10 minutes I heard snoring,” Rodgers said of his head coach. “Thursday, he misses an offensive meeting. Friday, he misses walkthrough... Saturday, he misses the team meeting.” Added Rodgers: “If you’re sleeping in meetings, you’re unhealthy.” The Steelers are 6-4 and have lost their last two games. On Tuesday night, the team announced that Rodgers would be inactive for the team’s game Friday against the Denver Broncos. The Steelers did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Rodgers’ interview. Rodgers blasted McCarthy while speaking to McAfee, alleging his coach even broke down a team huddle with a “one, two, three, Packers!” last week, confusing players. (McCarthy was previously Rodgers’s coach in Green Bay from 2006 to 2018.) “Everybody knows what’s going on. He’s missing walkthroughs, you don’t think everybody else knows?,” Rodgers said. “Does any other quarterback have these issues?” Rodgers added: “It’s a very delicate situation, the coaching staff is worried about their job security, the players are worried about their money and jobs security.” Rodgers said he is willing to speak out about McCarthy because of the financial security his long career has afforded him. Rodgers also claimed McCarthy hasn’t connected with Pittsburgh’s defense, and rebuffed Rodgers’ efforts to get him to connect with players on that side of the ball. Rodgers also said McCarthy has not been watching film and lacks an intimate knowledge of the team’s week-to-week game plans. “I don’t expect people to come out strong in my defense even though everybody knows the truth,” the quarterback said. Rodgers said issues with McCarthy began in training camp, and he also accused his coach of harboring ill will over his dismissal from the Packers. “In Mike’s mind, I got him fired in 2018. He told a staff member he still doesn’t forgive me for getting him fired in 2018,” Rodgers claimed. In the hours before his benching, Rodgers said he brought up his issues with McCarthy in an in-person conversation and delivered him an ultimatum to either address the problems or grant him a release. Rodgers claimed McCarthy did not admit to sleeping during team meetings, and the idea of his benching was not raised. “I found out that I was going to be inactive on a phone call last night from Pat Freiermuth,” Rodgers said, referring to the tight end. The quarterback repeatedly said his stories are not “hyperbole” or “opinion,” but instead first-hand accounts and facts. Rodgers does not expect to return to the Steelers. “There’s no going back, that ship has sailed.”

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers not returning to Steelers, says Mike McCarthy falls asleep in meetings and is 'unwell'
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers says Pat Freiermuth told him of his Steelers benching by phone as he ripped Mike McCarthy for snoring in meetings and saying "Packers."
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers said on Wednesday he's not going back to the Pittsburgh Steelers because "that ship has definitely sailed" and that was perhaps one of the least controversial things he said on Wednesday's "Pat McAfee Show" about his recent benching. Rodgers said he found out about the benching from teammate Pat Freiermuth, still has not heard from the team personally about a benching the club announced on social media on Tuesday night, and then he painted Mike McCarthy as a coach who skips meetings, falls asleep in meetings, and is "unwell." Rodgers laid bare a situation that has him at home on Wednesday while the rest of the team's players were at the facility preparing for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos. It was stunning. So much so, the Steelers planned to waive him after the interview took place. Rodgers said Freiermuth called him Tuesday night to give him the news he's benched. "I found out that I was gonna be inactive on a phone call last night from Pat Freiermuth," Rodgers said. AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY DISAGREEMENTS AT HEART OF QUARTERBACK'S BENCHING BY THE STEELERS Rodgers then went in on McCarthy. He portrayed him as someone who has fallen asleep in multiple quarterback meetings and snores, missed some meetings despite being the offensive play caller, and even broke down the team at halftime last week by chanting, "1, 2, 3 Packers," rather than the Steelers. "What are we doing?" Rodgers said. 'WHAT THE F--K, CALL IT!': AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY CURSE AT EACH OTHER DURING HOT MIC MOMENT Rodgers said he has joked "in the hallway" with general manager Omar Khan about McCarthy falling asleep in meetings. The quarterback destroying his head coach's reputation and professionalism on national television is a defining moment. There is no coming back from this, which is fine with Rodgers who said he is "not going back to Pittsburgh." That's fine because there is zero chance McCarthy, on behalf of the Steelers, would welcome Rodgers back on the team after this. Neither the coach nor the team has yet to respond, although a source confirmed the club would eventually release Rodgers. Rodgers said this issue has been in the works for weeks. "There are so many issues that I've been dealing with that ultimately led to where we're right now," Rodgers said. "Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring." "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers, we were all looking around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. Less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened." There's more from Rodgers: "Sunday we obviously struggled [against the Philadelphia Eagles] and the product wasn’t great," Rodgers said. "There were some guys early on that didn’t like the things we were doing, especially defensive guys. Mike didn’t want to get to know the defense. "At one point, I told him, ‘You should really lean into the defensive guys a little more and talk to those guys,’ and he said, ‘I don’t think I need to.’ Well, I said, I disagree with that. So, he kinda already lost a lot of those guys. "I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime, toward the end of it, we kinda (had the) offense on one side and defense on the other side, there’s some rambling or something and then, without even a heads-up, he says, ‘All right, 1, 2, 3, Packers!’ "That’s how he broke it down in the locker room." A Steelers' player confirmed to OutKick that indeed happened. Rodgers said he spoke with McCarthy on Monday "as a concerned friend." "It was, it was pretty wild because here I am, saying these things to him, I just told you, and he's denying all of it," Rodgers said. "Denying sleeping, like, Mike, there's five guys in the room that would sign an affidavit, admitting that what I just said is true. "So I'm not, there's no hyperbole. There's no, like, kind of stick it to you. It's like, you're unwell. And what's best for the team is you give it up to somebody, and you take care of yourself, and work on your health." These are not your father's or grandfather's Steelers. Those teams were stable. They had Chuck Noll coach the team for 23 years and win four Super Bowls. Then Bill Cowher coached for 15 years and won a Super Bowl. Then Mike Tomlin coached the team for 19 years, never had a losing season, and won a Super Bowl. But these Steelers? Not stable. They had a distracting Joey Porter contract hold-in during training camp and ended up trading a good player they drafted to the Dallas Cowboys. They had DK Metcalf lose his composure last week during the game against the Eagles, get ejected, and excused it. And then the Rodgers drama. None of this ends the way either party hoped in the offseason when McCarthy was hired, the coach worked to reunite with Rodgers after their years together in Green Bay, and Rodgers joined the team and said this would be his final NFL season. Not a happy ending for anyone. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Former Cowboys QB Defends Mike McCarthy After Aaron Rodgers' Explosive Interview
articles.summary: At least one of Mike McCarthy's former quarterbacks is sticking up for the head coach.
articles.body:
At least one of Mike McCarthy's former quarterbacks is sticking up for the head coach.

Ben DiNucci, who was with the Dallas Cowboys when McCarthy was the coach, took to social media Wednesday following Aaron Rodgers' shocking interview on The Pat McAfee Show and said he never personally witnessed some of the things the future Hall of Famer described:

Rodgers: McCarthy Said '1, 2, 3 Packers' in Huddle

Rodgers Claims McCarthy Fell Asleep in Meetings

James Harrison Backs Up Rodgers' Stories

For his part, Rodgers revealed during his discussion with McAfee he is not returning to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

He also criticized McCarthy for falling asleep in meetings, failing to get to know everyone on the team and struggling with game plans (h/t ESPN ).

It should be noted DiNucci made it clear he had quite a different relationship with McCarthy than Rodgers did since he was a young quarterback who was not the starter in Dallas. Rodgers, on the other hand, is a future Hall of Famer and one of the best signal-callers in NFL history.

Rodgers also has more experience with McCarthy considering they were together with the Green Bay Packers before this season in Pittsburgh.

Rodgers unleashed on McCarthy during the stunning interview and recounted times when the coach was "snoring" in meetings and even "broke it down" in the locker room by saying "one, two, three Packers" during the Steelers' loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

The quarterback continued and said McCarthy was "missing meetings" back in training camp, adding, "the word was he's sleeping and then he's sleeping in the coaches' film sessions and he's not alert here. And he doesn't want to get to know the defense."

He also said, "I think he learns the plan during the week. And multiple times he said that he doesn't watch film when I've talked to him on Tuesdays. He hasn't seen the film yet. Hadn't seen the film yet. I don't know how that's possible on a Tuesday after you play on a Sunday."

As for DiNucci, he surely wouldn't have been quite as intimately involved as Rodgers given the difference in their roles. However, he did appear in three games with one start for the Cowboys during the 2020 campaign.

Rodgers now joins DiNucci as a former quarterback of McCarthy, as NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the Steelers waived him following his interview with McAfee.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers gets absolutely humiliated, Curt Cignetti is fuming & Chiefs Heiress Gracie Hunt works in a lift
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers was benched for Mason Rudolph on Thanksgiving Eve, and reports say he skipped the Steelers facility as questions swirl behind the scenes.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Final Hump Day of November AND it's Thanksgiving Eve? Goodness gracious. How lucky are we? Wait ... there's also an NFL game tonight? On a holiday Wednesday? And it's a good one (on paper)? And we get more football tomorrow, Friday, Saturday, Sunday and Monday?! Come on. Are we blessed, or what? Let's roll. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where we now live in a world where Aaron Rodgers has been benched for Mason Rudolph. Didn't think I'd ever type that. Still not sure if it's real. The stupid autocorrect function tried to fix it three times before it finally let it go through. Even the woke AI bot doesn't believe it! AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY DISAGREEMENTS AT HEART OF QUARTERBACK'S BENCHING BY THE STEELERS What else? I've got the worst call of the college football season taking place last night in a #MACtion classic, Curt Cignetti went on a reposting SPREE after Indiana was dropped out of the college football playoffs, and Chiefs Heiress Gracie Hunt works in one final pre-Thanksgiving workout before the big day. This is how you meal prep, boys and girls. Take notes. OK, grab you an injector and a turkey, and settle in for one final November Hump Day 'Cap! Aaron Rodgers has stunk this year, but this is next-level humiliation This is a "put your hard hat on and try to stay under the radar so you can cut out early for the holiday" kind of day, so we're gonna keep this class short(ish) and sweet. We've got things to do and turkeys to prep. The big story of the day is Aaron Rodgers. Duh. I was STUNNED when I saw it come across my desk last night. "Aaron Rodgers benched for Mason Rudolph." I couldn't believe it. The first question that came to my mind? Is this the most humiliating thing that's ever happened to a future first ballot Hall of Famer? I'm serious. Think about it ... Reports are that Aaron didn't show up to the facility today, which isn't surprising. Obviously, there's been some sort of falling out behind the scenes. You don't bench Aaron Rodgers based on poor play alone. Something is stinky here, and I assume we'll all find out together over the next day or so. UPDATE: Aaron just went on McAfee and stuffed Mike McCarthy in a locker, which, frankly, is impressive. I've never seen anything like it. So, yes … falling out it is! Lordy. The Steelers, by the way, are a disaster. Rodgers hasn't looked great, but that team is horrible. Look at their remaining schedule. There is maybe one winnable game left. This is about to get nasty. But that's a story for another day. Right now, we're here to discuss Aaron Rodgers. He's become a lightning rod in recent years, but if you're old enough to remember him in his prime, there wasn't a better thrower of the ball (whatever that means) than Aaron Rodgers. What an incredible fall from grace: Is this the worst call of the college football season? I remember that playoff game like it was yesterday. One of the best playoff games of my lifetime. Again, nobody spun the rock quite like Aaron back in the day. Since then, it's been a disaster ... Two horrendous years with the Jets, followed by 18 disappointing months in Pittsburgh. And now, he's been benched. It HAS to be up there for biggest downfalls ... ever? Can you think of a superstar athlete who's career plummeted worse toward the end? I can't. Thoughts from any Steelers fans in class today? Let me know! Zach.Dean@OutKick.com. OK, let's leave the Aaron Rodgers humiliation ritual and head to something even worse that took place last night while you all were sleeping. Is this the worst call of the college football season? Cig & Gracie take us home I wrote about this monstrosity earlier, so feel free to check that out if you want to really get into the weeds. To me, it's just a horrible call. You don't make that call in that situation. Listen to that poor ESPN announcer. He's stunned. He's beside himself. He's looking for answers, and there's no ref in the booth to offer an explanation. The ball does seem to slightly move at first when it hits the receiver's face. It's slight, but it appears to move. He basically caught it with his facemask. Regardless, he still controls it before getting his first foot down. He then appears to get a second foot down just for good measure, although the back one may have been on the line. Does he lose control of it when he switches hands after the first foot hits? It looks like there's a slight chance of it, but I don't see it. It's certainly not nearly enough evidence to overturn a walk-off touchdown. He never lost control. That's three times since the 4 p.m. hour of NFL Sunday that refs have made just horrible calls. It's like we've all of a sudden just forgot what a catch is ... again. Did we ever figure it out? Probably not, but this was as bad a call as I can remember from this season. And buddy, there have been a TON of bad calls. I say it every week — officiating is at an all-time low right now. It's horrible. OK, let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day night. First up? We got another round of CFP rankings last night, and Indiana dropping out of the top-12 was the big development. Let's see how head coach Curt Cignetti handled the news: Nobody on the planet has been saltier over these rankings than Curt Cignetti. He's bashed them every single week, and the latest batch finally sent him over the edge. Now, I don't think Indiana is very good this year. I've said it all season, and I stand by it. BUT ... dropping the Hoosiers out of the top-12 after a 27-24 road loss to Washington is a bit much, no? Alabama is everyone's punching bag, right? Personally, I think 'Bama would dog-walk Indiana this year, but the numbers are the numbers, and the numbers say if Alabama's in, Indiana should probably be, too. See? I'm not completely blinded by the SEC. I can be fair! OK, that's it for today. This class is off tomorrow, so we'll see everyone bright and early Friday! Have a good Thanksgiving, everyone. Don't waste a single second tomorrow. Eat too much. Watch too much football. Play with the kids (or grandkids). When you're tired, go play some more. Crack a beer at 10 a.m. And another at 11. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP You've earned it. On the way out, here's Chiefs Heiress Gracie Hunt preparing her body for the big day. See y'all Friday. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers to be released by Pittsburgh Steelers after accusing head coach Mike McCarthy of 'sleeping in meetings'
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers claims that head coach Mike McCarthy was 'snoring' in a quarterback meeting in an explosive interview; Steelers are set to release the four-time NFL MVP; Rodgers had been benched after back-to-back losses with Mason Rudolph taking his place
articles.body:
Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show , Rodgers claimed that McCarthy had been "falling asleep in meetings" and insisted that the entire team felt a change was necessary following the veteran quarterback's decision to bench him for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos. Mason Rudolph is set to start in place of the four-time NFL MVP.

Pittsburgh confirmed in a statement that Rodgers would be "inactive", despite McCarthy having said on Monday that the 43-year-old remained the team's starting quarterback. Rodgers subsequently voiced his frustrations in a scathing interview, which has reportedly led to his release, according to US media reports.

"Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, and that word [benched] never even came up," Rodgers said on the ESPN sports talk show.

"I want to take you back through my last week, and this is not an abnormal week what I'm about to tell you, but these are some of the issues that I've been dealing with, which ultimately led to where we're at now.

"Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring.

"He woke himself up, was rattling his papers, we all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened.

"Thursday, he misses an offensive meeting. Friday, he doesn't come to the walkthrough. We only have a walkthrough, really, on Friday.

"He doesn't come to the protection walkthrough on Thursday. Saturday, he misses the morning meeting, and we don't have a team meeting Saturday night, for whatever reason, in Philly.

"Then comes to Sunday, when obviously we struggled and the product wasn't great. And there was some guys early on that didn't like the way things were going, especially defensive guys. And Mike didn't want to get in the middle of defense.

"At one point, I told him that he really needed to make more of an effort to connect with the defensive players and engage with them. His response was, 'Well, I don't think I need to.' I disagreed, and I think that attitude had already caused him to lose the support of a lot of those players.

"I think the final straw for many of us came at half-time. Towards the end of the team talk, with the offence on one side and the defence on the other, he was rambling. Then, without any warning or context, he suddenly shouted, 'One, two, three, Packers!'

"It was such a strange, out-of-the-blue moment. Nobody had even mentioned the Steelers; it was just an awkward, disjointed speech. But he said it loudly enough for everyone across the entire locker room to hear. It was one of those moments that really stuck with people.

"We all looked around going: 'What is going on? Where's his head at?'"

Rodgers is currently in his 22nd and final NFL season, having reunited with McCarthy after the pair previously won the Super Bowl together with the Green Bay Packers in 2010.

He also played a key role in McCarthy's appointment as Mike Tomlin's successor.

"We've had these conversations for months now, and it began as a concerned friend about somebody who's unhealthy," Rodgers continued.

"If you're sleeping in meetings, you're unhealthy. You're not coming to everything you should be. How many quarterbacks around the league are dealing with the same type of stuff?

"This guy's calling the plays. And so Monday we're having this conversation and I just said: We've got to make a change for the betterment of the team.'

"The entire team, and offensively think that a change is needed because they see it."

Rudolph has started only 19 games in seven seasons with the Steelers and the Tennessee Titans.

articles.title: 49ers' Shanahan Reacts to Brandon Aiyuk's Commanders Contract, 'They Got a Good Player'
articles.summary: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk's time with the San Francisco 49ers officially endafter the team released him on Monday, and he's now a member of the Washington Commanders' practice squad.
articles.body:
Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk's time with the San Francisco 49ers officially endafter the team released him on Monday, and he's now a member of the Washington Commanders' practice squad.

On Wednesday, Shanahan was asked for his thoughts regarding Washington's signing:

Aiyuk and the 49ers had an ugly and prolonged divorce , but the two sides have now parted ways.

San Francisco is doing well at 9-1, tied for the best record in the NFL with the Buffalo Bills. The 49ers have scored an NFL-high 31.6 points per game and look like a legitimate threat to win the Super Bowl.

Meanwhile, Aiyuk gets a chance to contribute in Washington, where he reunites with close friend, ex-Arizona State teammate and Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels. The 4-5-1 Commanders have won two straight and are in a fight for the NFC East, which is led by the 6-3-1 New York Giants.

Aiyuk hasn't played since Oct. 2024 , when he suffered a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus during a game against the Kansas City Chiefs.

There is no timetable for his return to the field, per Commanders head coach Dan Quinn, but he told reporters the wideout looked strong and fast when he worked out for the team.

"It'll take a lot of work to get to that spot to be ready and impact the team in a strong way," Quinn said, per ESPN's John Keim . "I'm excited to add him to the group. This is the type of competitor I love coaching, competing with and competing against. Let's get started."

Aiyuk also reunites with former 49ers front office executive Adam Peters, who is now the Commanders' general manager.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy's 'Ice Cream Sandwich' Assistant Detailed in NFL Rumors After Aaron Rodgers' Comments
articles.summary: It has been quite the Wednesday for Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, but he's at least reportedly got someone who can get him an ice cream sandwich if needed.
articles.body:
It has been quite the Wednesday for Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, but he's at least reportedly got someone who can get him an ice cream sandwich if needed.

Following Aaron Rodgers' explosive interview on The Pat McAfee Show in which he heavily criticized McCarthy, former NFL player Breiden Fehoko took to social media to reveal one Steelers player said the coach "has a personal assistant who brings him ice cream sandwiches on demand."

NFL insider Jordan Schultz said he spoke to multiple Steelers players, who confirmed the story:

Rodgers: McCarthy Said '1, 2, 3 Packers' in Huddle

Rodgers Claims McCarthy Fell Asleep in Meetings

James Harrison Backs Up Rodgers' Stories

It is yet another bizarre headline for McCarthy after Rodgers told McAfee he was done with the Steelers while also criticizing the coach for falling asleep in meetings, struggling to learn the game plan and failing to watch film, among other things (h/t ESPN ).

Rodgers also said he learned from teammate Pat Freiermuth he was being benched and detailed a moment during Pittsburgh's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles that McCarthy said, "one, two, three Packers" in the locker room.

McCarthy used to coach the Green Bay Packers when Rodgers was also the team's quarterback.

As for Rodgers, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the Steelers decided to waive him following the interview.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers claims Mike McCarthy slept through, missed meetings in Green Bay
articles.summary: Mike McCarthy slept through or missed meetings “for a decade” in Green Bay, according to the Packers’ former quarterback
articles.body:
I did not have former Green Bay Packers head coach Mike McCarthy's sleep patterns on my bingo card for "Thanksgiving Eve," but that's where Aaron Rodgers' appearance on The Pat McAfee Show took us on Wednesday. We're going to focus on the Packers-related news that Rodgers, who was benched and then later waived by the Pittsburgh Steelers this week, dropped today.

According to Rodgers, a tipping point in his relationship with McCarthy, now the head coach of the Steelers, was McCarthy breaking the locker room with a "1-2-3-Packers" chant against the Philadelphia Eagles last week, when Pittsburgh dropped the game 19-16 to fall to 6-4 on the season. That moment, per Rodgers, was an encapsulation of McCarthy's lack of preparedness — something that apparently stretches back to his days in Green Bay.

Rodgers claims that McCarthy has had issues with sleeping in meetings or missing meetings for well over a decade now:

Nobody knew it was going on for ten years in Green Bay. Even when I brought that up yesterday, his response was, "I fucking hate those coaches; that's why I didn't hire any of them in Pittsburgh." And I'm like, that's the worst response you could give. That's not even addressing the content of what I'm saying. I'm saying that you had unhealthy habits back then. We worked around it. I looked into what was going on in Dallas. Same exact stuff.

When discussing why he believed in McCarthy turning a corner in Pittsburgh, Rodgers stated that he didn't believe that McCarthy, a Yinzer, was "going to sleep through his dream job." He also noted that Packers head coach Matt LaFleur's schedule during the week is much different than McCarthy's approach.

In terms of blow-ups, Rodgers could only remember two periods in Green Bay that were touchy with McCarthy:

The only time we had it out was back in 2014, like behind closed doors, where it got really contentious. 2014 after the NFC Championship Game and I just asked him about his habits that week and he had missed multiple walkthroughs and meetings and post-practice stuff. Man, it got heated. It got heated in 2018 as well, after the Buffalo game. Same thing.

Worth mentioning: A former Packers teammate of Rodgers, linebacker A.J. Hawk, did not speak up to push back on the quarterbacks' stories from his time in Green Bay. You'd think that if Hawk didn't see these patterns of absence from McCarthy, he probably would have said something on Wednesday.

Since Rodgers' appearance, there have been a lot of reports that have supported what he said today.

Kalyn Kahler, currently of ESPN, referenced her 2018 piece for Sports Illustrated , where she mentioned that McCarthy would miss meeting in Green Bay. Nearly a decade later, she is adding that Rodgers brought up McCarthy sleeping through or missing meetings from a new source, a former Packer, who mentioned Rodgers bringing up these issues in both 2017 and 2018.

ESPN's Brooke Pryor, who covers the Steelers, claims multiple sources can vouch for Rodgers' "1-2-3-Packers" story.

Former Packers offensive lineman TJ Lang isn't exactly pushing back on Rodgers' stories, but is saying that a Rodgers of the past would have been against using the media in this way.

NFL reporter Jordan Schultz says at least one Steelers player is "happy it's out there," and added that McCarthy has an ice cream sandwich assistant.

articles.title: 49ers activate Nate Hobbs, re-sign Brandin Cooks to practice squad
articles.summary: Cornerback Nate Hobbs has not played in a game since signing with the 49ers in March, but that could change against the Seahawks this weekend.
articles.body:
Cornerback Nate Hobbs has not played in a game since signing with the 49ers in March, but that could change against the Seahawks this weekend.

Hobbs was activated from injured reserve on Wednesday as part of a handful of roster moves announced by the team. Hobbs landed on the list on September 1 with a groin injury and was at the end of his 21-day window to be activated.

The 49ers opened a roster spot by placing offensive tackle Colton McKivitz on injured reserve. He will miss the rest of the season after fracturing and dislocating his ankle last Sunday.

The 49ers also announced that they have re-signed wide receiver Brandin Cooks to their practice squad. He was dropped from the active roster ahead of the Niners' Week 11 win over the Vikings.

articles.title: Cris Collinsworth is out for Browns-Raiders. Here’s who replaces him
articles.summary: Cris Collinsworth won’t call Browns-Raiders on Sunday Night Football. See why he’s out and who will join Mike Tirico in the NBC booth Sunday.
articles.body:
There will be a different voice in the booth when the Cleveland Browns host the Las Vegas Raiders on "Sunday Night Football." Cris Collinsworth will be off Sunday, with Jason Garrett replacing him alongside Mike Tirico, according to NBC Sports .

The change is part of NBC's unusual Thanksgiving week schedule. Collinsworth and Tirico will call the Buffalo Bills-Kansas City Chiefs game Thursday night. Tirico will then work Sunday's game with Garrett as the analyst, while Melissa Stark reports from the sideline, NBC Sports announced Tuesday .

It is not the first Thanksgiving week that Garrett has filled Collinsworth's seat. Yahoo Sports reports that this will be the fourth Thanksgiving week game Garrett has called with Tirico in place of Collinsworth.

Garrett is a familiar face to NFL viewers. The former Dallas Cowboys head coach now works for NBC and regularly appears on "Football Night in America." Yahoo Sports notes that Garrett coached Dallas from 2011 through 2019.

The Browns-Raiders game was not originally scheduled for prime time. The NFL flexed the Cleveland-Las Vegas matchup into "Sunday Night Football." The move gives Cleveland a national spotlight late in the season.

Sunday will also mark a rare moment for Browns fans. NBC says it will be Cleveland's first home "Sunday Night Football" game since 2019 . Coverage begins at 7 p.m. ET, with kickoff scheduled for 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock.

articles.title: Dennis Allen on how Jeffery Simmons has impacted Bears defense
articles.summary: Dennis Allen discussed how Jeffery Simmons has impacted the defense ahead of the Bears' Thanksgiving game against the Lions.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears made a franchise-defining move trading for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons this season, and his impact has already been massive in just a short span, further elevating Chicago as Super Bowl contenders.

In just three games with the Bears , Simmons already has five sacks, which is more than he had in the seven games he played in with the Tennessee Titans before the trade. Chicago had six sacks in their Week 11 win against the New Orleans Saints. They also have 13 sacks in the past three games.

Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has always been creative in his playcalling. However, Simmons gives him even more freedom because Chicago can now get pressure on the quarterback without having to send an extra rusher.

32 NFL QBs (including Bears' Caleb Williams) ranked by QBR in Week 12

"In each and every game, we have a game plan going in, and then really it comes down to a feel of when you feel like you need to bring the extra rusher and what you feel like you can still affect the quarterback with a four-man rush," Allen said. "It's a good problem to have as a play caller knowing that you don't have to rush five, six, seven guys to be able to get to the quarterback. It's comforting to know that when you call a four-man rush, more often than not the quarterback's not going to be just standing there patting the ball."

Unfortunately, Allen lost one of his favorite blitzers, cornerback Kyler Gordon, who is currently dealing with a shoulder injury. In the four games Gordon has played in so far this year, he has blitzed 14 times and has four sacks, including three in his season debut against the Atlanta Falcons.

The Bears will need to get creative on defense to stop running back Jahmyr Gibbs and the rest of the Detroit Lions offense on Thanksgiving. Chicago has not defeated the Lions since the 2023 season, although Detroit does not have the best track record on Thanksgiving. It will also be their first matchup against the Bears this season. Both teams come into the game 8-2; the winner will take sole possession of first place in the NFC North.
